sections.title: Enums and match
sections.text:
## Enums and match

```lox
enum Color { Red, Green, Blue }
enum Shape { Circle(Float), Rect(Float, Float) }

val s: Shape = Shape.Circle(2.0)
val area = match s {
  Shape.Circle(r) => 3.14 * r * r
  Shape.Rect(w, h) => w * h
}
```

- `enum Name { Variant, Variant(Type, ...) }` declares a closed type; variants have a
  **positional** payload and are accessed with a namespace (`Color.Green`,
  `Shape.Circle(1.0)`). Enums are declared at the top of the program.
- Enums may be generic (`enum Pair[A, B]`); `Result[T, E]` is built in, with
  `Result.Ok(T)`/`Result.Err(E)`, and cannot be redefined. `Option` remains `T?`.
- Type: `Shape`, `Result[Int, String]`; arguments are invariant. `is`/`as` accept an enum
  without arguments (`x is Color`); with arguments they are rejected (the runtime erases `T`).
- `match` is an **expression**: `match e { Pattern => expr ... }`. v1 patterns:
  `Name.Variant`, `Name.Variant(a, b)` (positional bindings) and `_`. Arms are separated
  by a line, `;` or `,`; using `match` as a statement discards the result.
- Exhaustiveness is **mandatory**: all variants covered or `_`; a missing one is an error
  (`Non-exhaustive match; missing Shape.Rect.`); a duplicate variant/arm after `_` is
  `Unreachable match arm.` The scrutinee must be an enum (not `Any`/union).
- Pattern bindings have the payload type (`Result.Ok(v)` → `v: T`); the type of `match`
  is the union of the arms. Without `--check`, a `match` with no matching arm is a runtime error
  (`No match arm matched.`).
- Equality is structural (enum, variant and payload); `print(Color.Green)` →
  `Color.Green`, `print(Shape.Circle(1.0))` → `Shape.Circle(1.0)`. Enums are not iterable,
  have no `len` and are not `Map` keys.
- Outside v1: literal/`nil` patterns, guards, nesting, `|`, `match` on unions and
  null variants of a generic enum. The backend rejects `enum`/`match` until L6.

sections.title: Exceptions
Errors
sections.text:
## Errors

| Phase | When | Exit code (file) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| lexical/syntax/resolver | before executing | **65** |
| runtime | during execution | **70** |
| file not found | before everything | **66** |

- Compilation format: `file:line:col: error[CODE]: message` + a snippet with a caret
  (`human`) or only the header (`short`); catalog and JSON envelope in
  [`erros.md`](https://loxia-lang.github.io/loxia/reference/errors/) ([ADR-0075](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0075-diagnosticos-estruturados.md)).
- Runtime format: `file:line:col: error[CODE]: message` (no caret, same as the binary).
- Messages are in English (compatibility with the book and tests).
- Compile errors are **accumulated** (the parser tries to recover; the resolver reports
  all of them), ordered by `(file, offset, code)`, without duplicates and limited by
  `--max-errors`; runtime errors stop at the first one.
- Error codes are stable; columns, spans, JSON, stack trace, `fixes[]`, provenance
  `notes` and LSP exist
  ([ADR-0075](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0075-diagnosticos-estruturados.md),
  [ADR-0089](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0089-stack-trace-de-runtime.md),
  [ADR-0099](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0099-notas-de-proveniencia.md),
  [ADR-0090](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0090-lsp-escopo-e-hospedagem.md)).
- In the REPL, each line starts with a clean error state and the environment remains.

sections.title: Deliberate differences from the book
sections.text:
## Deliberate differences from the book

- Division by zero is an error (the book returns `inf`).
- The REPL accepts an optional trailing `;` and prints the value of expressions.
- `return` at the top level is a compile error as early as ch. 11 (in the book, the resolver does this).
- Numbers are separate `Int` and `Float` (the book uses only `float`); `/` is always `Float`,
  `%` is truncated and `Int` wraps — see [ADR-0006](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0006-int-float-separados.md).
- `val`/`var` do not exist in the book (which has only mutable `var`); see [ADR-0005](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0005-val-var-imutabilidade.md).
- `for x in` and `Range` (`0..10`) do not exist in the book; see
  [ADR-0007](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0007-ranges-e-iteracao.md).
- `List[T]` (literal, indexing, `push`/`pop`, `len` and structural equality) does not exist in the
  book; see [ADR-0015](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0015-listas-tipadas.md).

Everything else follows the book's jlox, including the messages.

sections.title: Modules
sections.text:
## Modules

### stdlib T1

> Per-module reference, generated from the signatures/doc comments and the builtins
> registry: [`../stdlib/`](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/stdlib).

- `std.strings`: `isEmpty`, `isBlank`, `trim`/`ltrim`/`rtrim`, `startsWith`/`endsWith`,
  `contains`/`indexOf`/`lastIndexOf`, `split`/`splitLines`/`lines`/`words`,
  `repeat`, `upper`/`lower`/`capitalize`, `reverse`, `count`, `replaceFirst`/`replaceAll`,
  `slice`, `padStart`/`padEnd`.
- `std.lists`: `isEmpty`, `length`, `map`, `filter`, `each`, `fold`, `reduce`, `any`,
  `all`, `none`, `find`, `findIndex`, `contains`, `indexOf`, `reverse`, `take`, `drop`,
  `slice`, `sum`, `first`, `last`, `count`, `min`, `max`, `getOr`.
- `std.maps`: `entries`/`toList` (`(String, V)` pairs), `fromEntries`, `merge` (the right
  one wins), `pick`, `omit`, `mapValues`, `filterKeys`, `filterValues`, `invert`
  (`Map[String, String]`), `hasValue`, `getOr`. The API is `Map[String, V]`: the checker
  does not yet express generic key constraints (post-MVP); `Int`/`Bool` keys use
  the language methods.
- `std.numeric`: `gcd`/`lcm`, `isPrime`/`primes`, `factorial`, `powMod`, `digitSum`,
  `isEven`/`isOdd`/`sign`, `mean`/`median`/`mode`/`variance`/`stddev` (statistics of
  `List[Int]`; an empty list returns `nil`; population variance) and
  `roundTo`/`toBase`/`fromBase` (base 2..36). An invalid domain (negative `factorial`,
  base out of range) raises `RuntimeError`; invalid `fromBase` returns `nil`.
- `std.asserts`: `assert`, `assertEq`, `assertNotNil` (returns the narrowed value) and
  `fail`; the failure is a `RuntimeError`, catchable by `except RuntimeError as e`.
- `std.results`: `isOk`/`isErr`, `map`/`mapErr`, `unwrapOr`, `andThen` and `toOptional`
  for `Result[T, E]`. Since `andThen` receives `fn(T) -> Result[U, E]`, a lambda that
  constructs `Result.Ok`/`Result.Err` does not infer the generic enum yet; use a named
  function with an annotated return (post-MVP checker gap).
- `lists.sort(xs, compare)` requires `compare: fn(T, T) -> Int` (negative/zero/positive),
  is stable and returns a new list. `sortBy`/`groupBy` do not exist yet.
- `lists.zip`, `flatten`, `flatMap`, `unique`, `chunk` and `partition` are generic;
  `partition` returns `(yes, no)`.
- These functions are pure Lox over the kernel; they are deterministic and enter the T1 corpus.

### stdlib T2

The T2 modules are pure Lox over the kernel and add no syntax
([ADR-0079](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0079-stdlib-t2.md)). The deterministic ones enter the `t2` corpus; the
**ambient** ones ([ADR-0072](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0072-stdlib-batteries.md) §5) are outside I1 and have tests
with fixed input.

- `std.json`: `parse(text) -> Any`, `stringify(value) -> String` and
  `pretty(value, indent = 2) -> String`. Objects become `Map[String, Any]` (insertion
  order), arrays become `List[Any]`, `Int`/`Float` are distinct and `null` becomes `nil`.
  Invalid JSON also becomes `nil`; nesting above 16 is invalid. `stringify`
  raises `RuntimeError` for a non-finite `Float` or a value that is not JSON.
- `std.fmt`: `format(template, List[Any])` with `{}` and `{{`/`}}`, `pad(text, width,
  fill = " ")` (on the left), `commas`, `fixed(value, digits)`, `percent(value, digits = 0)`
  and `bytes(n)` (B/KiB/MiB/GiB/TiB). No locale; extra/missing arguments and `fixed` outside
  0..15 raise `RuntimeError`.
- `std.bytes`: `Builder` (incremental byte a byte over `List[Int]`; `push`, `pushByte`,
  `len`, `build`), `ChunkBuilder` (whole `Bytes` chunks with balanced concatenation; better
  for large blocks), `compare` (lexicographic, returns -1/0/1), encoders `u16be`/`u16le`/
  `u32be`/`u32le`/`u64be`/`u64le` and decoders `readU16be`/`readU16le`/`readU32be`/
  `readU32le`/`readU64be`/`readU64le` (the 64-bit helpers use the two's-complement bit
  pattern; decoders return `Int?`, nil when the bytes do not fit). Pure and deterministic;
  in the `t2` corpus.
- `std.paths` (POSIX, lexical, does not touch the disk): `join` (an absolute second argument wins,
  without normalizing), `dirname`, `basename`, `ext`/`stem` (a leading dot does not count as an
  extension), `normalize` (collapses slashes, resolves `.`/`..`), `isAbsolute` and `split`.
- `std.fs` **ambient**: `readText -> String?`, `readLines -> List[String]?` (drops the
  final newline), `writeText -> Bool`, `appendText -> Bool` (reads and rewrites; creates the
  file if absent), `exists -> Bool` and `listDir -> List[String]?` (sorted, without
  `.`/`..`, `nil` if it is not a readable directory). `File.readBytes(n)` reads up to `n`
  raw bytes (`Ok(nil)` at EOF), without UTF-8 validation.
- `std.io`: `write`/`writeErr` (deterministic), `readLine -> String?`, `readAll ->
  String` and `prompt(message) -> String?` (writes and reads a line); reading is ambient.
  Input that is not valid UTF-8 is a `RuntimeError` (without a traceback), not corrupted text.
- `std.cli`: `parse(args, spec) -> Map[String, Any]` with `spec` as a `List[String]` of
  `flag:NAME`, `option:NAME` and `positional:NAME` entries; accepts `--name value`,
  `--name=value` and `--`; flags become `Bool`, options/positionals become `String` or `nil`.
  `flag`/`option`/`positional` read the result and `usage(program, spec)` generates the text.
  Invalid usage (unknown option, missing value, flag with a value) is a `RuntimeError`.
- `std.sets`: `Set[T]` with `add`, `has`, `remove` (returns `Bool`, no error if absent),
  `len`, `toList` (insertion order), `union`, `intersect`, `difference` and
  `fromList(List[T])`. The internal field is `Map[Any, Bool]`: `T` must be `String`, `Int`
  or `Bool` at runtime; `Set[Float].add` fails with the `Map` key error (generic
  constraints are post-MVP).
- `std.csv`: `parse(text) -> List[List[String]]?` (RFC 4180; accepts CRLF/LF, quotes with
  `""`, newlines inside a field; `nil` if malformed) and `stringify(rows) -> String` (CRLF,
  final newline, quoting when needed; an empty list generates empty text and an empty row is
  an error).
- `std.utf8`: `byteLen(text) -> Int` (UTF-8 bytes), `utf16Len(text) -> Int` and
  `utf16Column(text, index) -> Int` (UTF-16 width of the prefix of `index` code points,
  limited to `0..len(text)`). Pure Lox over `charCodeAt`, deterministic, in the `t2` corpus.
- `std.proc` **ambient** (POSIX, [ADR-0095](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0095-processos-streams-poll.md)):
  `Stream` (`read`, `write`, `close`), `Process` (`stdin`/`stdout`/`stderr`, `wait`,
  `kill`, `close`), `Output` (`code`, `stdout`, `stderr`), `spawn(argv) -> Process?` and
  `run(argv, stdin = "", timeoutMs = 0) -> Output?`. No shell; `run` drains stdout/stderr
  with `poll`, kills on timeout and returns `nil`; `stdin` has the practical limit of the pipe
  buffer (~64 KiB). Outside the I1/I3 corpus.
- `std.iter`: `enumerate(items)`, `zip(left, right)`, `sum(List[Int])`,
  `sumFloat(List[Float])`, `contains`, `any`, `all` and `find` (the first match or `nil`).
  The `Step[T]` enum (`Step.Item(value)`) allows iterating `nil` elements:
  `next() -> Step[T]?` terminates on `nil` and the body matches `Step.Item(value)`.
- `std.rand`: `Rand(seed)` (xorshift64*), `nextInt`, `int(min, max)` inclusive,
  `float` in `[0, 1)`, `bool` and `shuffle(items, r)`; deterministic by seed.
- `std.log` **ambient**: `Level` enum (`Debug`/`Info`/`Warn`/`Error`) and `Logger`, which
  writes `[LEVEL] message` to stderr; no timestamp.
- `std.hash`: `fnv1a32`, `fnv1a64` and `djb2` over the **UTF-8 bytes**; `sha256(text) ->
  String` (hex) and `sha256Bytes(Bytes) -> Bytes` (raw 32 bytes) are the cryptographic
  digests. The 64-bit fnv returns the bit pattern in i64 (it may be negative).
- `std.collections`: generic `Stack`, `Queue`, `Deque` and `PriorityQueue` (heap with an
  explicit comparator `fn(T, T) -> Bool`).
- `std.timex` **UTC-only**: `daysFromCivil`, `civilFromDays`, `iso`, `parseIso` (strict,
  returns `Int?`), `addDays` and `parts`; no timezone and no clock.
- `std.property` ([ADR-0098](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0098-property-based-testing.md)): `Gen[T]` with
  `generate`/`shrink`, `forAll(gen, check, runs = 100, seed = 0)` and generators
  `int`, `intRange`, `bool`, `float`, `stringOf`, `listOf[T]` (with
  `listOfInt`/`listOfString` as aliases) and `oneOf`; a failure shrinks the counterexample and
  reports the seed.
- `std.test` ([ADR-0096](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0096-testes-biblioteca-e-runner.md)): `Suite` (explicit state,
  because a module does not accept top-level `var`) with `describe`, `it` (runs immediately),
  `beforeEach`/`afterEach` (scoped to `describe`; outer→inner `before`,
  inner→outer `after`, even on failure), `skip`, `report` (TAP + 0/1) and `done`
  (`os.exit(report())`); matchers `expect` (`toBe`/`notToBe`), `expectGt/Ge/Lt/Le`
  (`T: Ord`), `expectNil`/`expectNotNil`, `expectList`/`toContain`,
  `expectString`/`contains`, `expectRaise`; `TestFailure`/`Skip` and `Recorder`. No
  reflection/registry; `--filter=`/`--only=` and `--list` (only prints `# test <name>`) come
  from `args()`. The test body is `fn() -> Nil`; an unhandled exception becomes `not ok`.
- `std.convert`: `toInt`/`toFloat` (`T?`), `toBool` (`"true"`/`"false"`),
  `base64Encode/Decode` and `hexEncode/Decode`. They are text-based and operate on the
  UTF-8 bytes of the text; decoding bytes that are not valid UTF-8 (or malformed text)
  returns `nil`. Hex is lowercase. For raw binary use `Bytes`/`std.bytes`.

Instance fields may have a container type (`List`, `Map`, tuple, `Range`, enum) since
ADR-0079; `Any` as a field is not yet supported by the backend.


- A module is a `.lx` file; a folder is a path namespace, not a module.
- Modules contain only imports, `fn`, `class` and `enum`; no `val`/`var` or top-level
  statement. Import is static, with no initialization order.
- `import m`/`import m as x` creates a namespace; `from m import name [as y]` binds public names.
- A top-level name starting with `_` is private to the module; outside it `_x` is an error, including
  through the namespace (`m._x`).
- `std.` resolves in the bundle; user modules are relative to the project root.
- Without `loxia.toml`, the root is the entry's directory. With a manifest, the root is the manifest
  folder and the order is: project → dependencies → `[modules].paths` → `--module-path` →
  `std` ([ADR-0100](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0100-dependencias-path.md)).
- `[dependencies] acme = { path = "../acme" }` makes `import acme.foo` look for
  `../acme/foo.lx` (the package name is not the directory name). The path is relative to the
  manifest and must exist; `std` is a reserved name and `import acme` alone is an error.
- `loxia.lock`, next to the manifest, pins each dependency by name, origin, optional
  `[package].version` (`X.Y.Z`) and the `sha256` of its `.lx` tree ([ADR-0104](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0104-lock-e-frozen.md)).
  It is generated by `loxia lock` (canonical bytes: entries sorted by name, fixed key order,
  relative posix paths, no timestamp) and verified by `loxia lock --check` (exit `1` when
  stale) and `loxia fetch`.
- `--frozen` resolves dependencies only from the lock: a missing lock (when dependencies
  exist), a missing/extra package, or a different path/version/hash is an error `C0002`
  (exit 65). Without `--frozen`, `path` dependencies are read live from disk.
  `--offline` forbids the network and `--cache-dir` selects the dependency cache
  (default `.loxia/cache/` in the project root). `run`, `check`, `build`, `ast` and `test`
  never access the network; only `loxia lock` and `loxia fetch` may, and `--offline`
  forbids it there too. Only the root manifest declares dependencies: the lock is flat,
  `std` and `[modules].paths` never appear in it.
- A git dependency is `acme = { git = "https://github.com/acme/acme", rev = "v1.2.3" }`
  ([ADR-0105](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0105-dependencias-git.md)). `rev` is required and is a full commit or a
  tag (never a branch); exactly one of `path`/`git` is allowed. `loxia lock` resolves the tag
  to a commit and records `git`, `rev`, `commit`, `version` (required in the dependency's
  `loxia.toml`) and the tree `sha256`. `loxia fetch` populates the cache (bare mirror plus a
  clean `git archive` checkout, no `.git`/hooks/submodules); `run`/`check`/`build` use the
  locked commit only and fail with `C0002` when the checkout is missing ("run `loxia fetch`").
  `--offline` restricts `lock`/`fetch` to the cache, and `file://` URLs are dev/test only and
  stored verbatim in the lock.
- A dependency imports its own package by name (`acme.base`) or another declared
  dependency; it does not see the project or `[modules].paths`. `[modules].paths` are loose
  roots (vendor/monorepo): `import shared.util` resolves `<root>/shared/util.lx`.
- `..` and absolute paths remain forbidden in `import`; they only appear in the manifest
  `path` or in `--module-path`. The same module in two roots is an **ambiguity error**
  (never “first wins”), with relative paths in the diagnostic.
- No `*`, no re-export and no module as a value.
- A module is **pure by construction**: only top-level declarations, so importing executes no
  effect; an unused import is `W1002` and removing the line is `safe` (fix).

### stdlib T1

> Per-module reference, generated from the signatures/doc comments and the builtins
> registry: [`../stdlib/`](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/stdlib).

- `std.strings`: `isEmpty`, `isBlank`, `trim`/`ltrim`/`rtrim`, `startsWith`/`endsWith`,
  `contains`/`indexOf`/`lastIndexOf`, `split`/`splitLines`/`lines`/`words`,
  `repeat`, `upper`/`lower`/`capitalize`, `reverse`, `count`, `replaceFirst`/`replaceAll`,
  `slice`, `padStart`/`padEnd`.
- `std.lists`: `isEmpty`, `length`, `map`, `filter`, `each`, `fold`, `reduce`, `any`,
  `all`, `none`, `find`, `findIndex`, `contains`, `indexOf`, `reverse`, `take`, `drop`,
  `slice`, `sum`, `first`, `last`, `count`, `min`, `max`, `getOr`.
- `std.maps`: `entries`/`toList` (`(String, V)` pairs), `fromEntries`, `merge` (the right
  one wins), `pick`, `omit`, `mapValues`, `filterKeys`, `filterValues`, `invert`
  (`Map[String, String]`), `hasValue`, `getOr`. The API is `Map[String, V]`: the checker
  does not yet express generic key constraints (post-MVP); `Int`/`Bool` keys use
  the language methods.
- `std.numeric`: `gcd`/`lcm`, `isPrime`/`primes`, `factorial`, `powMod`, `digitSum`,
  `isEven`/`isOdd`/`sign`, `mean`/`median`/`mode`/`variance`/`stddev` (statistics of
  `List[Int]`; an empty list returns `nil`; population variance) and
  `roundTo`/`toBase`/`fromBase` (base 2..36). An invalid domain (negative `factorial`,
  base out of range) raises `RuntimeError`; invalid `fromBase` returns `nil`.
- `std.asserts`: `assert`, `assertEq`, `assertNotNil` (returns the narrowed value) and
  `fail`; the failure is a `RuntimeError`, catchable by `except RuntimeError as e`.
- `std.results`: `isOk`/`isErr`, `map`/`mapErr`, `unwrapOr`, `andThen` and `toOptional`
  for `Result[T, E]`. Since `andThen` receives `fn(T) -> Result[U, E]`, a lambda that
  constructs `Result.Ok`/`Result.Err` does not infer the generic enum yet; use a named
  function with an annotated return (post-MVP checker gap).
- `lists.sort(xs, compare)` requires `compare: fn(T, T) -> Int` (negative/zero/positive),
  is stable and returns a new list. `sortBy`/`groupBy` do not exist yet.
- `lists.zip`, `flatten`, `flatMap`, `unique`, `chunk` and `partition` are generic;
  `partition` returns `(yes, no)`.
- These functions are pure Lox over the kernel; they are deterministic and enter the T1 corpus.

  (exit 65). Without `--frozen`, `path` dependencies are read live from disk.
  `--offline` forbids the network and `--cache-dir` selects the dependency cache
  (default `.loxia/cache/` in the project root). `run`, `check`, `build`, `ast` and `test`
  never access the network; only `loxia lock` and `loxia fetch` may, and `--offline`
  forbids it there too. Only the root manifest declares dependencies: the lock is flat,
  `std` and `[modules].paths` never appear in it.
- A git dependency is `acme = { git = "https://github.com/acme/acme", rev = "v1.2.3" }`
  ([ADR-0105](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0105-dependencias-git.md)). `rev` is required and is a full commit or a
  tag (never a branch); exactly one of `path`/`git` is allowed. `loxia lock` resolves the tag
  to a commit and records `git`, `rev`, `commit`, `version` (required in the dependency's
  `loxia.toml`) and the tree `sha256`. `loxia fetch` populates the cache (bare mirror plus a
  clean `git archive` checkout, no `.git`/hooks/submodules); `run`/`check`/`build` use the
  locked commit only and fail with `C0002` when the checkout is missing ("run `loxia fetch`").
  `--offline` restricts `lock`/`fetch` to the cache, and `file://` URLs are dev/test only and
  stored verbatim in the lock.
- A dependency imports its own package by name (`acme.base`) or another declared
  dependency; it does not see the project or `[modules].paths`. `[modules].paths` are loose
  roots (vendor/monorepo): `import shared.util` resolves `<root>/shared/util.lx`.
- `..` and absolute paths remain forbidden in `import`; they only appear in the manifest
  `path` or in `--module-path`. The same module in two roots is an **ambiguity error**
  (never “first wins”), with relative paths in the diagnostic.
- No `*`, no re-export and no module as a value.
- A module is **pure by construction**: only top-level declarations, so importing executes no
  effect; an unused import is `W1002` and removing the line is `safe` (fix).

pages.title: Errors
pages.summary: Catalog of what the interpreter reports today, with phase and consequence. Messages are in English; CLI text remains in Portuguese, and this documentation is in English. The decision behind the format is in the ADR-0075.

sections.title: Format and exit codes
sections.text:
## Format and exit codes

Every compilation diagnostic has a **stable code** (`error[E3001]`), a position and, in the
`human` format, a source snippet with a caret:

```
example.lx:3:7: error[E2001]: Already a variable with this name in this scope.
  |
3 |   var a = 2;
  |       ^
```

| Phase | `human` format | Exit code |
| --- | --- | --- |
| lexical | `file:line:col: error[E0xxx]: message` + caret | 65 |
| syntax | `file:line:col: error[E1xxx]: message` + caret | 65 |
| resolver | `file:line:col: error[E2xxx]: message` + caret | 65 |
| checker (`--check`) | `file:line:col: error[E3xxx]: message` + caret | 65 |
| backend | `file:line: error[E4xxx]: message` (no column/caret) | 65 |
| runtime | `file:line:col: error[R1xxx]: message` (no caret) | 70 |
| CLI/timeout | `error[C0001]: message` (no location) | 124 |
| missing file | `Erro: Arquivo 'x' não encontrado.` (stderr) | 66 |

Backend internal errors (`E4002`) are prefixed with `internal lowering error:` or
`internal error:`; `E4001` is reserved for declared gaps (`... is not supported by
the backend yet.`). C compiler failures are sanitized so temporary paths are not leaked.

- `human` (default) shows header + snippet; `short` shows only the header; `json` shows
  the v1 envelope; `--json-lines` emits `start`/`diagnostic`/`summary` per line. Flags:
  `--error-format=human|short|json`, `--json`, `--color=auto|always|never` (respects
  `NO_COLOR`) and `--max-errors N` (default 20; `0` = unlimited).
- **Warnings** (`W1xxx`, today `W1001` local never read) have `severity: warning`, exit 0 and
  appear in the `summary`; `-Werror` turns them into an error (exit 65) only in `check`/`build`.
  `run` does not emit warnings to preserve I1 (the binary does not have them).
- `--timeout=MS` applies to `run`/`check`; the timeout is `C0001` + exit 124. `--watch` only in
  `check`; changes re-emit diagnostics with an incremental `revision`.
- Compilation errors go to **stderr** (`check`'s JSON goes to stdout). In `run`, stdout is the
  program's; in `build --emit=ll`, stdout is the IR's — that is why the JSON of these commands
  stays on stderr.
- Compilation (lexing, parser, resolver and checker): the program **does not execute**. The
  parser recovers (`synchronize`) and the resolver walks the whole AST, so one run can list
  several errors; they come out sorted by `(file, offset, code)` and without duplicates.
- Runtime: stops at the **first** uncaught error. Without `try`, the error is **fatal**
  (exit 70) and whatever was already printed remains ([ADR-0026](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0026-freeze-1.0.md)).
  Inside `try`, the error becomes a catchable `RuntimeError` and `except ... as e` exposes
  `e.message` and `e.site` (`file:line:column` of the throw, `""` when unknown)
  ([ADR-0042](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0042-excecoes.md), [ADR-0120](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0120-localizacao-de-falha-em-excecoes.md));
  `Result` is the explicit alternative for expected errors
  ([ADR-0041](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0041-enums-match.md)). The runtime uses the
  **same header** as compilation (`file:line:col: error[CODE]:`), without a caret — the
  binary can run without the source. When the position is synthetic (internal field), the
  header degrades to `error[CODE]: message`. After the header come the stack trace
  frames ([ADR-0089](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0089-stack-trace-de-runtime.md)).
- In the REPL there is no exit code; the line with the error is discarded and the session
  continues. The file is `<repl>`.
- The displayed path is relative to the CWD; if the file is outside the CWD, only the basename.
  An absolute path never appears (I3). `std.*` modules use the logical name
  (`std/strings.lx`) so as not to depend on the CWD or collide with a user file.
- A **compilation** error in a module points to the module's file, with a snippet and caret for
  that file: the token carries the origin, so the checker and the resolver do not inherit the
  entry file. The **runtime** error also points to the module, because the frame carries the
  function's file (ADR-0089).

### Runtime stack trace

An uncaught runtime error prints, after the header, one frame per Lox activation (innermost
first). The name is the function's display name (`f`, `init`, `<lambda>`, `C` in the
constructor) and the position is the **call site** — where that activation was called:

```text
mod.lx:2:12: error[R1002]: Division by zero not allowed
  at inner (main.lx:7:14)
  at outer (main.lx:9:3)
```

- The innermost frame is the one that was executing the error; its position is the call that
  activated it. The top (script code) is not a frame.
- More than 10 frames: it shows the **5 innermost**, a line
  `  ... N frames omitted` and the **5 outermost** (`TRACE_HEAD`/`TRACE_TAIL` in
  [`limits.py`](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/loxia_core/execution/limits.py)). The trimming is deterministic.
- `--error-format=short` keeps one line per diagnostic and **omits** the frames; `json`
  exposes them in `trace` (`frames[]`, `omitted`, `head`). In the binary the format is always
  the human one.
- The runtime error in a module points to the function's file (not the entry one). A caught
  exception prints nothing; `raise;` re-raises from the point of the `raise`.
- `R1015` has a position: the declaration of the function whose activation overflowed
  ([ADR-0089](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0089-stack-trace-de-runtime.md), which revisits
  [ADR-0077](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0077-limite-de-pilha.md)).

### Labels, notes and help

The model already had `labels`, `notes` and `help`; now they have producers in resolution and
checker errors. `E2001` (duplicate variable) and `E2002` (assignment to `val`) point to the
previous declaration with a second snippet (`-`):

```text
dup.lx:3:7: error[E2001]: Already a variable with this name in this scope.
  |
3 |   val a = 2
  |       ^
  |
2 |   val a = 1
  |       - first declared here
```

`E3003` (undefined name) gains `help` when there is a close visible name — the suggestion is
deterministic (sorted candidates) and ignores mangled module symbols:

```text
suggestion.lx:2:7: error[E3003]: Undefined variable 'nam'.
  |
2 | print(nom)
  |       ^^^
help: did you mean 'name'?
```

**Type** errors gain a provenance note when the value has a name or path
(`Variable`, `Get`, `Index`, `Call`) and the caret points to the destination — the variable
name, the call parenthesis, the `=`. The note shows the source text and the line of the
**start of the expression**, normalized to one line and truncated at 80 characters
([ADR-0099](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0099-notas-de-proveniencia.md)):

```text
provenance.lx:6:5: error[E3001]: Expected Int, found String.
  |
6 | val total: Int = person.name
  |     ^^^^^
note: the value comes from `person.name` (line 6)
```

The note covers annotated `val`/`var`, destructuring, field, `return`, assignment, call
arguments, `len`/`chars`/`math.*`, list index and map key/value. Literals and compound
expressions do not get a note (it would only repeat the caret); without the source loaded,
no note is emitted. Arity, undefined name, property and runtime errors do not use
provenance.

`--error-format=short` remains one line (without labels/notes/help); `json` always includes
all three. A label without the source loaded degrades to `note: file:line:col: message`.

### JSON envelope (v1)

`schema_version` is an integer and changes only on a breaking change. `span.start`/`end` are
half-open; `column` is 1-based in code points and `offset` is 0-based in UTF-8 bytes.
`summary.suppressed` counts the diagnostics cut by `--max-errors`.

```json
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "command": "check",
  "success": false,
  "exit_code": 65,
  "diagnostics": [
    {
      "code": "E2001",
      "phase": "resolver",
      "severity": "error",
      "message": "Already a variable with this name in this scope.",
      "span": {
        "file": "example.lx",
        "start": { "line": 3, "column": 7, "offset": 24 },
        "end": { "line": 3, "column": 8, "offset": 25 }
      },
      "labels": [],
      "notes": [],
      "help": null,
      "trace": null,
      "fixes": []
    }
  ],
  "summary": { "errors": 1, "warnings": 0, "suppressed": 0 }
}
```

`fixes` is an additive list (it may stay empty): each item has `applicability`
(`safe`/`unsafe`), `message` and `edits[]` with `span` + `new_text`. W1001/W1002 and local
E3004 emit `safe`; E3003, E2001, E2002, E2009, E3002, E3015, E3016, E3018 and E3004 in a
public API emit `unsafe`; `safe` is only applied automatically when there is proof of
behavior preservation
([ADR-0093](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0093-cli-agent-friendly-e-reparo.md), analysis in
[`tech/fixes.md`](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/tech/fixes.md)).

`trace` is `null` outside the runtime; in a runtime error it has the frames already trimmed:

```json
"trace": {
  "frames": [
    { "name": "f", "file": "main.lx", "line": 7, "column": 14 }
  ],
  "omitted": 0,
  "head": 0
}
```

sections.title: Codes
sections.text:
## Codes

Codes identify **families**, not messages; they are never reused and the catalog is
closed (emitting a code outside this list does not compile). The checker's long tail uses
`E3000` until it is refined into more specific codes. The per-phase tables below are
**generated** from `loxia_core/diagnostics/codes.py` (`make codes`); do not edit them by hand.

| Range | Phase | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `E0xxx` | lexical | scanner |
| `E1xxx` | syntax | parser |
| `E2xxx` | resolver | scopes and declarations |
| `E3xxx` | checker | types and semantics |
| `E4xxx` | backend | lowering/emission |
| `R1xxx` | runtime | interpretation and binary |

<!-- codes:start -->
### Lexicon

| Code | Family |
| --- | --- |
| `E0001` | unexpected character |
| `E0002` | unterminated string |
| `E0003` | invalid string escape |
| `E0004` | invalid numeric literal (separator or literal overflow) |
| `E0005` | unterminated block comment |
| `E0006` | unterminated interpolation |
| `E0007` | invalid Unicode escape |

### Syntax

| Code | Family |
| --- | --- |
| `E1001` | unexpected token (the `Expect …` family) |
| `E1002` | invalid assignment target (including `?.` in assignments) |
| `E1003` | limit of 255 parameters/arguments |
| `E1004` | invalid declaration (`val` without initializer, non-constant default, …) |
| `E1005` | invalid type annotation (`List`/`Map` arity, union in `is`, generic) |
| `E1006` | invalid literal (map at the start of a statement) |
| `E1007` | invalid `match` |

### Resolver

| Code | Family |
| --- | --- |
| `E2001` | duplicate variable in scope |
| `E2002` | assignment to `val`/immutable parameter |
| `E2003` | invalid `return` (top level or value in `init`) |
| `E2004` | `this` outside a class |
| `E2005` | `super` outside a class or without a superclass |
| `E2006` | invalid inheritance (class inherits from itself) |
| `E2007` | field conflict (duplicate or with a method) |
| `E2008` | local read in its own initializer |
| `E2009` | assignment to a `val` field |
| `W1001` | local declared and never read (warning) |
| `W1002` | import declared and never used (warning) |

### Checker

| Code | Family |
| --- | --- |
| `E3000` | generic semantic error (checker fallback) |
| `E3001` | type mismatch |
| `E3002` | call arity |
| `E3003` | undefined name (variable, property or field) |
| `E3004` | missing annotation |
| `E3005` | unknown type, class or superclass |
| `E3006` | value is not callable |
| `E3007` | invalid operands |
| `E3008` | invalid list (common type, empty element, index) |
| `E3009` | invalid map (key, common type) |
| `E3010` | invalid iteration |
| `E3011` | generic type inference |
| `E3012` | generic feature not supported yet |
| `E3013` | invalid cast |
| `E3014` | builtin/reserved name redefined |
| `E3015` | override/method conflict |
| `E3016` | field not initialized |
| `E3017` | invalid declaration (type param, enum, `init`) |
| `E3018` | missing return on some path |
| `E3019` | `math.*` argument |
| `E3020` | type arguments (generic/enum/class arity) |
| `E3021` | not supported by the interpreter |

### Backend

| Code | Family |
| --- | --- |
| `E4001` | not supported by the backend yet |
| `E4002` | backend internal error/verification/link |
| `E4003` | generic instantiation budget exceeded |

### Runtime

| Code | Family |
| --- | --- |
| `R1000` | generic runtime error |
| `R1001` | value is not callable |
| `R1002` | division or modulo by zero |
| `R1003` | undefined variable |
| `R1004` | undefined property, field or variant |
| `R1005` | runtime arity |

| `R1007` | index out of bounds |
| `R1008` | key not found in map |
| `R1009` | assignment to immutable binding |
| `R1010` | uncaught exception |

| `R1013` | field not initialized |
| `R1014` | invalid value (map key, superclass, …) |
| `R1015` | call depth above the limit |

### CLI

| --- | --- |

| `C0003` | project scaffolding (existing target, conflict, git) |
| `C0004` | manifest edit refused (unsupported shape, conflict) |

## Lexical

sections.title: Syntax
sections.text:
## Syntax

Messages in the `Expect … .` pattern; the most common ones:

| Message | When |
| --- | --- |
| `Expect expression.` | `primary` found no start of expression |
| `Expect expression; '//' is integer division, and comments start with '#'.` | `//` where an expression is expected (it is not a comment) |
| `Type unions in 'is' need parentheses: 'is (A \| B)'.` | `x is Int \| String` without parentheses in the union |
| `Unexpected ':'. Map literals can't start a statement; use 'val m = { ... }' or parentheses.` | `{ "a": 1 }` at the start of a statement |
| `Expect end of interpolation.` | leftover token after the `${...}` expression |
| `Expect 'else' after conditional expression.` | ternary without `else` |
| `Expect property name after '?.'.` | `a?.` without a name |
| `Can't assign through optional chaining.` | `a?.b = 1` |
| `Expect ';' after expression.` | bare expression without `;` on the same line |
| `Expect ';' after variable declaration.` | `var`/`val` without `;` on the same line |
| `Expect ';' after return value.` | `return` followed by another statement on the same line (before `}` or a new line, the `;` is optional) |
| `Expect ';' after loop condition.` | `for` without `;` in the condition |
| `Expect ')' after for clauses.` | `for` without `)` |
| `Expect ')' after if condition.` | `if`/`elif` without `)` |
| `Expect ')' after condition.` | `while` without `)` |
| `Expect ')' after arguments.` | call without `)` |
| `Expect ')' after expression.` | grouping without `)` |
| `Expect '(' after ...` | `for`, `if`, `while`, function/method declaration |
| `Expect '{' before function body.` / `method body.` | function without `{` |
| `Expect '{' before class body.` | class without `{` |
| `Expect '}' after block.` / `after class body.` | block/class without `}` |
| `Expect variable name.` | `var`/`val` without an identifier |
| `Expect initializer for 'val' declaration.` | `val x;` without `=` |
| `Expect function name.` / `method name.` | `fn`/method without a name |
| `Expect parameter name.` | missing parameter |
| `Expect class name.` | `class` without a name |
| `Expect superclass name.` | `class B(` without a name |
| `Expect ')' after superclass.` | `class B(A` without `)` |
| `Expect ';' after field declaration.` | field without `;` |
| `Field initializer must be a constant.` | `var x = 1 + 2;` in the class body |
| `Default value must be a constant.` | `fn f(x = 1 + 2)` |
| `Required parameter can't follow an optional parameter.` | `fn f(a = 1, b)` |
| `Variadic parameter must be last.` | `fn f(...xs, y)` |
| `Type aliases can't be generic yet.` | `type BoxAlias[T] = ...` |
| `Spread argument must be last.` | `f(...xs, 2)` |
| `Expect '.' after 'super'.` | `super` without a dot |
| `Expect superclass method name.` | `super.` without a name |
| `Expect property name after '.'.` | `obj.` without a name |
| `Expect index expression.` | `xs[]` |
| `Expect ']' after index.` | `xs[0` without `]` |
| `Expect ']' after list elements.` | `[1, 2` without `]` |
| `List expects 1 type argument(s), got 0.` | `val xs: List = [];` |
| `Unknown generic type 'list'. Did you mean 'List'?` | `list[int]` (lowercase name) |
| `Invalid assignment target.` | `1 = 2`, `f() = 3` |
| `Can't have more than 255 arguments.` | giant call |
| `Can't have more than 255 parameters.` | giant function |

sections.text:
## Resolver

| Message | When |
| --- | --- |
| `Already a variable with this name in this scope.` | `val`/`var` repeated in the same scope; parameter + local; repeated parameter |
| `'x' is immutable; declare it with 'var' to allow assignment.` | assignment to a local `val` or immutable parameter (compilation) |
| `Can't read local variable in its own initializer.` | `{ var a = a; }` |
| `Can't return from top-level code.` | `return` outside a function |
| `Can't return a value from an initializer.` | `return value;` inside `init` |
| `Can't use 'this' outside of a class.` | `this` outside a method |
| `A class can't inherit from itself.` | `class A(A)` |
| `Can't use 'super' outside of a class.` | `super.m` outside a class |
| `Can't use 'super' in a class with no superclass.` | `super.m` in a class without a superclass |
| `Field 'x' already declared.` | field repeated in the same body or in the subclass |
| `Field 'x' conflicts with a method.` | field and method with the same name |
| `Can't assign to immutable field 'x'.` | `this.x = ...` of a `val` field outside `init` |

sections.title: Runtime
sections.text:
## Runtime

| Message | When |
| --- | --- |
| `Undefined variable 'x'.` | read/assignment of a nonexistent name |
| `'x' is immutable; declare it with 'var' to allow assignment.` | assignment to a global `val` |
| `Can't redeclare immutable variable 'x'.` | redeclaring a global `val` **or a builtin** (`len`, `str`, `repr`, `range`) |
| `Operand must be a number.` | `-"a"` |
| `Operand must be an integer.` | `~1.0` |
| `Operands must be numbers.` | `1 < "a"` |
| `Operands must be integers.` | `1.0 & 1`, `7 // 2.0`, `1 << 2.0` |
| `Operands must be two numbers or two strings.` | `1 + "a"` |
| `Division by zero not allowed` | `/ 0` or `// 0` |
| `Modulo by zero not allowed` | `% 0` |
| `Negative exponent not allowed for integer power.` | `2 ** -1`; use `2.0 ** -1` |
| `Invalid exponentiation.` | `0.0 ** -1.0`, `(-1.0) ** 0.5` |
| `Exponentiation overflow.` | `1e308 ** 2` |
| `Integer overflow.` | `--debug` with `9223372036854775807 + 1`; exit 70 |
| `Can't cast this Float to Int.` | `math.sqrt(-1.0) as Int` (NaN/Inf/out of range) |
| `Can't cast value to Int.` | `"1" as Int` at runtime |
| `math.floor() requires a finite Float in Int range.` | `math.floor(1e100)`; same for ceil/round/trunc |
| `math.floor() expects numbers.` | `math.floor("1")` at runtime |
| `Shift count must be between 0 and 63.` | `1 << 64`, `1 >> -1` |
| `Can only call functions and classes.` | `1()` |
| `Expected N arguments but got M.` | fixed arity of a function/class |
| `Expected at least N arguments but got M.` | short call with defaults |
| `Expected N to M arguments but got K.` | long call with defaults |
| `Only instances have properties.` | `1.x` |
| `Only instances have fields.` | `1.x = 2` |
| `Undefined property 'x'.` | nonexistent field/method; nonexistent `super.x` |
| `Undefined field 'x'.` | assignment to an undeclared field |
| `Field 'x' must be initialized.` | instance created without initializing the field |
| `Can't assign to immutable field 'x'.` | second assignment to a `val` field |
| `Superclass must be a class.` | `class B(A)` with `A = 1` |
| `Only lists and maps can be indexed.` | `xs[i]`/`xs[i] = v` with a value that is neither a list nor a map |
| `List index must be an integer.` | `xs["0"]` |
| `List index N out of bounds for length M.` | negative index or `>= len(xs)` |
| `Can't pop from an empty list.` | `[].pop()` |
| `Can't modify a list while iterating over it.` | `for x in xs { xs.push(x) }` |
| `Map keys must be strings, integers or booleans.` | `m[1.5]`, `{1.5: 1}`, `m[nil]` |
| `Key not found in map.` | `m["missing"]`, `m.remove("missing")` |
| `Duplicate key in map literal.` | `{"a": 1, "a": 2}` |
| `Can't modify a map while iterating over it.` | `for k in m { m["b"] = 2 }` |
| `len() expects a string, a list or a map.` | `len(3)` |
| `Can only iterate over a range, a list, a map or a string.` | `for x in 42` |
| `iter() must return an instance with next() -> T?.` | `iter()` returns a non-instance |
| `iter() must take no arguments.` / `next() must take no arguments.` | protocol with parameters |

The immutability message appears in **two phases**: compilation for locals/parameters
(65) and runtime for globals (70). The text is the same on purpose.

| Message | When |
| --- | --- |
| `Expected X, found Y.` | assignment/argument/return/field with an incompatible type |
| `Unknown type 'X'.` / `Unknown superclass 'X'.` | annotation with a nonexistent name |

| `Undefined variable 'x'.` / `Undefined property 'x'.` / `Undefined field 'x'.` | nonexistent name |
| `Can't assign to immutable field 'x'.` | `val` field outside `init` |

| `List index must be an integer, found X.` | `xs["0"]` in `--check` |

| `Expected a string, a list or a map, found X.` | `len(3)` in `--check` |
| `Can't infer type argument(s) 'T'.` | generic call without a context/argument that determines `T` |
| `Can't infer type argument 'T' from Any.` | `Any` argument for a `T` parameter |
| `Recursive type inferred for 'T'.` | `T` would be `List[T]` etc. |

| `Generic methods aren't supported yet.` | `get[T] (...)` in a class |

sections.title: How to test
sections.text:
## How to test

- Golden cases in [`tests/cases/errors/`](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/tests/cases/errors) use the markers
  `# expect error:` (65) and `# expect runtime error:` (70). The runner ignores the snippet's
  code lines when matching the message, so that an `# expect` on the same line as the code does
  not turn into a false positive. See [skill `lox-testing`](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/.dsh/skills/lox-testing/SKILL.md).
- `tests/test_diagnostics.py` covers the model and the three renderers without capturing stderr;
  `tests/test_determinism.py` requires identical bytes across seeds.

sections.title: What is still missing
sections.text:
## What is still missing

Already implemented: `Diagnostic` model, stable codes, spans (line/column/offset),
`human`/`short`/`json`, dedup/ordering/cap, deterministic relative path, the same runtime
header in the interpreter and in the binary
([ADR-0075](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0075-diagnosticos-estruturados.md)), stack trace
([ADR-0089](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0089-stack-trace-de-runtime.md)), provenance `notes`
([ADR-0099](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0099-notas-de-proveniencia.md)), fixes/warnings/JSONL
([ADR-0093](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0093-cli-agent-friendly-e-reparo.md)) and LSP
([ADR-0090](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0090-lsp-escopo-e-hospedagem.md)).

No open diagnostic work item: `E3004` closed with a fix conditioned on the exact
type ([`../tech/fixes.md`](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/tech/fixes.md)); what remains of tooling lives in
[`../roadmap.md`](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/roadmap.md).

pages.title: Guarantees — what the language promises
pages.summary: This page is the contract with whoever uses the language (or builds tooling on top of it). It does not describe syntax or semantics — that is in lexicon, syntax, semantics and errors. Here live the promises that survive new features.

sections.title: The four guarantees
sections.text:
## The four guarantees

| # | Guarantee | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **I1** | Same program, same result: the interpreter **is** the specification | 🟡 covers the declared corpus (table below) |
| **I2** | Nothing happens implicitly | ✅ holds today |
| **I3** | Observable determinism: same input ⇒ same bytes | ✅ holds today and is tested in CI |
| **I4** | Clean `--check` ⇒ the backend compiles (or refuses only the declared gap) | ✅ holds today and is tested in CI |

### I1 — Executable equivalence

The tree-walk is the **normative definition** of the language. Every program in the declared
corpus must produce the **same stdout (bytes)**, the **same stderr** and the **same exit code**
in both engines; if they diverge, the bug is in the backend.

The corpus is the entire conformance corpus, **annotated and classified by level** in
`tests/corpus_manifest.py`. Each case is in `LEVELS` (the backend compiles and agrees),
`PENDING` (the `--check` passes, the backend still refuses with **65** and the message
`... is not supported by the backend yet.`) or `NEGATIVE` (fails on purpose in the
`--check`). A case only enters `LEVELS` when the three channels match; promotion is
monotonic and the differential test never compares against a hand-written expectation. The
`PENDING` list is public: it is the honest record of what is missing, not a secret.

<!-- levels:start -->
| Level | Cases that compile and agree (I1) |
| --- | --- |
| `l0` | 4 |
| `l1` | 3 |
| `l2` | 14 |
| `l2.5` | 4 |
| `l3` | 14 |
| `l4` | 12 |
| `l5` | 30 |
| `l6` | 72 |
| `k0` | 2 |
| `t1` | 6 |
| `t2` | 20 |
| `t3` | 7 |
| `t7` | 3 |

**191 cases** across 13 levels compile and agree; **1 in `PENDING`** (`bytes_method_value` (l6)); **6 negative** on purpose.
<!-- levels:end -->

Levels not yet implemented reject with an **explicit compilation error**
(exit 65), never with silent lowering.

The comparison is per channel: when stdout and stderr go to the **same** descriptor
(`2>&1`), the interleaving order of the two outputs is not part of the guarantee.

There is no promise that interpreted and compiled code have the same **speed**
or the same memory consumption. The same observable result includes **stderr byte for byte**,
so the runtime stack trace is also identical in both engines
([ADR-0089](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0089-stack-trace-de-runtime.md)).

#### Engine layers: core, ambient and native-only

I1 covers **core**: features whose semantics both engines implement and that are in the
corpus. Two other layers are declared, and neither promises equivalence
([ADR-0128](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0128-contrato-de-motores.md)):

| Layer | Promise | Runs on | Refusal |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **core** | I1 + I3, in the corpus | interpreter and native | — |
| **ambient** | outside I1/I3; fixed-input tests | wherever the host allows | denied by `--sandbox` when it is a host capability |
| **native-only** | no equivalence promise; binary semantics only | `--emit=exe` | **the interpreter refuses at compile time** |

The three labels are a **projection of two independent axes**: determinism (`ambient`) and
engine support (`native_only`). A capability may be native-only and ambient at the same time
(a thread) or native-only and deterministic (pure SIMD); the label only decides the display,
never the promise.

A native-only capability is **refused**, never silently different:

```
error[E3021]: `sqlite.createFunction` is not supported by the interpreter; build with `--emit=exe`.
```

The refusal is a compilation error (exit 65), points at the call site and happens before any
execution. `loxia check` is engine-agnostic and accepts every layer; `run`/REPL refuse
native-only, and `build` only refuses the declared backend gap (`E4001`, I4). The layer of
every public primitive is published by `loxia capabilities --json`.

#### Stack budget ([ADR-0077](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0077-limite-de-pilha.md))

The binary and the tree-walk count **Lox activations** (function, method, lambda, `init` and
constructor) against the same limit: **10,000 calls**. Call 10,001 is `R1015`
(`Stack overflow.`), exit 70, catchable by `try`/`except RuntimeError`, with the position of the
callee's declaration and the stack trace of the active frames. Native calls and built-in
exception constructors do not count. Constructor + `init` count as two activations.

- The binary reserves a 128 MiB stack soft limit (`setrlimit`) before running; the
  declared budget is 64 MiB. On platforms with a smaller hard limit, the limit is clamped.
- The tree-walk raises `sys.setrecursionlimit` to 200,000 (internal budget, not a
  contract).
- Above 10,000 calls the error is deterministic and the trace is trimmed (5 innermost + 5
  outermost + elision), with no address/time in the output.

#### Memory budget ([ADR-0074](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0074-gc-boehm-e-contrato-de-memoria.md), [ADR-0087](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0087-heap-cap-e-self-hosting.md))

The binary uses a conservative **Boehm GC**, with a **default hard cap of 512 MiB** of collected
heap (ADR-0074 set 128 MiB; ADR-0087 raised the default). Exceeding the cap is `exit 70`
+ `Out of memory.` on stderr, without a traceback, and the ceiling does **not** depend on the
environment.

- The build can choose another ceiling with `--max-heap=SIZE` (only `--emit=exe`; default `512M`,
  range `32M..8G`). The value is embedded in the binary; it is neither an env var nor a runtime flag.
- **I1 covers programs whose peak live memory fits in 64 MiB**. Above that, the
  program is outside the corpus: it may run (up to the cap), but there is no guarantee of result
  or of failure point. Self-hosting is declared outside I1 until its own corpus exists.
- The interpreter has **no** ceiling (Python GC) and can run programs that the binary
  refuses — the asymmetry is declared.
- Because Boehm is conservative, the **exact point** at which a program above the cap overflows
  is not deterministic: false roots depend on the stack and on ASLR. What is stable is the
  channel, the message and the exit code. Programs that print before overflowing do not have the
  stdout prefix covered by I1.

#### Monomorphization budget ([ADR-0063](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0063-orcamento-monomorfizacao.md))

The native backend monomorphizes generics; each specialization costs code. Per compilation:

- at most **256** specialized functions and **256** specialized class layouts;
- generic type nesting up to **8** constructors;
- a mangled generic name up to **1024 bytes**.

Exceeding any limit is a declared backend gap, not a type error: exit 65, code `E4003`, and
no partial object/binary. The checker still accepts the program and the tree-walk is
unaffected. The initial limits were validated against the corpus and a synthetic nesting
case (max 15 functions/4 classes/depth 1 in the corpus; the ceiling costs ~1.2 MiB and
~0.33 s locally); see [`bench/README.md`](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/bench/README.md).

### I2 — Nothing happens implicitly

No conversion, coercion, truncation, rounding, truthiness or fallback happens
without being written in the code.

```lox
print(1 + 2.0)      # 3.0  — Int -> Float promotion, arithmetic only
print(1 + "1")      # error — no coercion between number and string
print(4 / 2)        # 2.0  — `/` is always Float
print(-7 // 2)      # -3   — truncated
print(1 == 1.0)     # true — numeric equality with promotion
print(1 == "1")     # false — different types are never equal
if ("") { print("empty is truthy") }  # prints: only nil and false are falsy
print((nil ?? 0))   # 0    — `??` replaces nil only
print(3.9 as Int)   # 3    — explicit cast, truncated
```

In **storage** there is no promotion: `val x: Float = 2`, `x = 2`, `f(2)` and `return 2` in a
`-> Float` function are type errors; write `2.0` or `2 as Float`
([ADR-0059](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0059-i4-check-limpo-compila.md)).

If you want the conversion, it is written: there is no "the compiler sorts it out".

### I3 — Observable determinism

Same input + same flags ⇒ **same bytes** of output and of diagnostics. This holds for
stdout, stderr, exit code and `--dump-ast`. The following are forbidden in the output: memory
address, PID, timestamp, absolute path, `set`/`dict` order, locale and directory order.

The 1.0 prelude does not read the clock or other ambient inputs: `clock` was removed
([ADR-0026](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0026-freeze-1.0.md)). The **ambient functions** declared in
[ADR-0072](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0072-stdlib-batteries.md) §5 — `args`, `os.getenv`, `time.now`,
`time.sleep`, `std.fs`, `std.io` reads, `std.proc`/`process.*` and kernel
file opening — are explicitly **outside** this guarantee and the differential corpus; they
have their own test with fixed input. `std.fs.listDir` sorts entries by byte precisely so as
not to leak the directory order.

**Streaming (not I3, it is an I/O contract):** `io.write`/`io.writeErr` flush on every
call in both engines, and `io.flush()` forces both channels. `print` follows the stdio
buffer (block on a pipe, line on a tty) — as in the oracle. Without the flush, a process that
reads another's output (pipe, JSONL, MCP, LSP) hangs waiting for bytes that stay in the buffer
([ADR-0094](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0094-kernel-io-flush-e-read-utf8.md)); the
`test_io_write_flush_antes_de_bloquear_no_stdin` test polices this, because the byte comparison
at the end of the process does not distinguish "flushed" from "flushed on exit".

The implemented `math.*` is deterministic: `abs`, `min`, `max`, `clamp`, `floor`, `ceil`,
`round`, `trunc` and `sqrt`. `log`, `exp`, `sin`, `cos`, `tan` and `pow` depend on libm and
stay **outside** 1.0/I3 ([ADR-0029](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0029-conversoes-math.md)). `--debug` changes
overflow behavior by design; the guarantee holds for the same flags.

```bash
./lox program.lx > a.txt 2>&1   # twice, on different machines/flags
./lox program.lx > b.txt 2>&1
cmp a.txt b.txt                   # identical
```

The wording of an error message **may change between versions**; the exit code does not
(`65` compilation, `70` runtime). Diagnostic **codes** are stable and never
reused ([ADR-0075](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0075-diagnosticos-estruturados.md)); the output is sorted
by `(file, offset, code)`, deduplicated, limited by `--max-errors` and the displayed path
is always relative. The JSON carries `schema_version`.

### I4 — Clean `--check` ⇒ it compiles

Every program that passes `--check` compiles. The **only** acceptable refusal in lowering is the
gap already declared and classified:

```
... is not supported by the backend yet.
```

Any other error after a clean check is an I4 violation. The checker is the **source of
truth** for types; the backend consumes the published types and does not invent its own rule.

```bash
uv run main.py --check prog.lx      # exit 0 …
uv run main.py --emit=exe prog.lx   # … so this compiles (or refuses only "not supported")
```

It is the operational corollary of I1: without it, the same program could give `2` in the
interpreter and a type error in the compiler, with the user receiving two contradictory
diagnostics ([ADR-0059](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0059-i4-check-limpo-compila.md)).

sections.title: I1 — Executable equivalence
sections.text:
### I1 — Executable equivalence

The tree-walk is the **normative definition** of the language. Every program in the declared
corpus must produce the **same stdout (bytes)**, the **same stderr** and the **same exit code**
in both engines; if they diverge, the bug is in the backend.

The corpus is the entire conformance corpus, **annotated and classified by level** in
`tests/corpus_manifest.py`. Each case is in `LEVELS` (the backend compiles and agrees),
`PENDING` (the `--check` passes, the backend still refuses with **65** and the message
`... is not supported by the backend yet.`) or `NEGATIVE` (fails on purpose in the
`--check`). A case only enters `LEVELS` when the three channels match; promotion is
monotonic and the differential test never compares against a hand-written expectation. The
`PENDING` list is public: it is the honest record of what is missing, not a secret.

<!-- levels:start -->
| Level | Cases that compile and agree (I1) |
| --- | --- |
| `l0` | 4 |
| `l1` | 3 |
| `l2` | 14 |
| `l2.5` | 4 |
| `l3` | 14 |
| `l4` | 12 |
| `l5` | 30 |
| `l6` | 72 |
| `k0` | 2 |
| `t1` | 6 |
| `t2` | 20 |
| `t3` | 7 |
| `t7` | 3 |

**191 cases** across 13 levels compile and agree; **1 in `PENDING`** (`bytes_method_value` (l6)); **6 negative** on purpose.
<!-- levels:end -->

Levels not yet implemented reject with an **explicit compilation error**
(exit 65), never with silent lowering.

The comparison is per channel: when stdout and stderr go to the **same** descriptor
(`2>&1`), the interleaving order of the two outputs is not part of the guarantee.

There is no promise that interpreted and compiled code have the same **speed**
or the same memory consumption. The same observable result includes **stderr byte for byte**,
so the runtime stack trace is also identical in both engines
([ADR-0089](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0089-stack-trace-de-runtime.md)).

#### Engine layers: core, ambient and native-only

I1 covers **core**: features whose semantics both engines implement and that are in the
corpus. Two other layers are declared, and neither promises equivalence
([ADR-0128](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0128-contrato-de-motores.md)):

| Layer | Promise | Runs on | Refusal |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **core** | I1 + I3, in the corpus | interpreter and native | — |
| **ambient** | outside I1/I3; fixed-input tests | wherever the host allows | denied by `--sandbox` when it is a host capability |
| **native-only** | no equivalence promise; binary semantics only | `--emit=exe` | **the interpreter refuses at compile time** |

The three labels are a **projection of two independent axes**: determinism (`ambient`) and
engine support (`native_only`). A capability may be native-only and ambient at the same time
(a thread) or native-only and deterministic (pure SIMD); the label only decides the display,
never the promise.

A native-only capability is **refused**, never silently different:

```
error[E3021]: `sqlite.createFunction` is not supported by the interpreter; build with `--emit=exe`.
```

The refusal is a compilation error (exit 65), points at the call site and happens before any
execution. `loxia check` is engine-agnostic and accepts every layer; `run`/REPL refuse
native-only, and `build` only refuses the declared backend gap (`E4001`, I4). The layer of
every public primitive is published by `loxia capabilities --json`.

#### Stack budget ([ADR-0077](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0077-limite-de-pilha.md))

The binary and the tree-walk count **Lox activations** (function, method, lambda, `init` and
constructor) against the same limit: **10,000 calls**. Call 10,001 is `R1015`
(`Stack overflow.`), exit 70, catchable by `try`/`except RuntimeError`, with the position of the
callee's declaration and the stack trace of the active frames. Native calls and built-in
exception constructors do not count. Constructor + `init` count as two activations.

- The binary reserves a 128 MiB stack soft limit (`setrlimit`) before running; the
  declared budget is 64 MiB. On platforms with a smaller hard limit, the limit is clamped.
- The tree-walk raises `sys.setrecursionlimit` to 200,000 (internal budget, not a
  contract).
- Above 10,000 calls the error is deterministic and the trace is trimmed (5 innermost + 5
  outermost + elision), with no address/time in the output.

#### Memory budget ([ADR-0074](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0074-gc-boehm-e-contrato-de-memoria.md), [ADR-0087](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0087-heap-cap-e-self-hosting.md))

The binary uses a conservative **Boehm GC**, with a **default hard cap of 512 MiB** of collected
heap (ADR-0074 set 128 MiB; ADR-0087 raised the default). Exceeding the cap is `exit 70`
+ `Out of memory.` on stderr, without a traceback, and the ceiling does **not** depend on the
environment.

- The build can choose another ceiling with `--max-heap=SIZE` (only `--emit=exe`; default `512M`,
  range `32M..8G`). The value is embedded in the binary; it is neither an env var nor a runtime flag.
- **I1 covers programs whose peak live memory fits in 64 MiB**. Above that, the
  program is outside the corpus: it may run (up to the cap), but there is no guarantee of result
  or of failure point. Self-hosting is declared outside I1 until its own corpus exists.
- The interpreter has **no** ceiling (Python GC) and can run programs that the binary
  refuses — the asymmetry is declared.
- Because Boehm is conservative, the **exact point** at which a program above the cap overflows
  is not deterministic: false roots depend on the stack and on ASLR. What is stable is the
  channel, the message and the exit code. Programs that print before overflowing do not have the
  stdout prefix covered by I1.

#### Monomorphization budget ([ADR-0063](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0063-orcamento-monomorfizacao.md))

The native backend monomorphizes generics; each specialization costs code. Per compilation:

- at most **256** specialized functions and **256** specialized class layouts;
- generic type nesting up to **8** constructors;
- a mangled generic name up to **1024 bytes**.

Exceeding any limit is a declared backend gap, not a type error: exit 65, code `E4003`, and
no partial object/binary. The checker still accepts the program and the tree-walk is
unaffected. The initial limits were validated against the corpus and a synthetic nesting
case (max 15 functions/4 classes/depth 1 in the corpus; the ceiling costs ~1.2 MiB and
~0.33 s locally); see [`bench/README.md`](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/bench/README.md).

sections.title: I2 — Nothing happens implicitly
sections.text:
### I2 — Nothing happens implicitly

No conversion, coercion, truncation, rounding, truthiness or fallback happens
without being written in the code.

```lox
print(1 + 2.0)      # 3.0  — Int -> Float promotion, arithmetic only
print(1 + "1")      # error — no coercion between number and string
print(4 / 2)        # 2.0  — `/` is always Float
print(-7 // 2)      # -3   — truncated
print(1 == 1.0)     # true — numeric equality with promotion
print(1 == "1")     # false — different types are never equal
if ("") { print("empty is truthy") }  # prints: only nil and false are falsy
print((nil ?? 0))   # 0    — `??` replaces nil only
print(3.9 as Int)   # 3    — explicit cast, truncated
```

In **storage** there is no promotion: `val x: Float = 2`, `x = 2`, `f(2)` and `return 2` in a
`-> Float` function are type errors; write `2.0` or `2 as Float`
([ADR-0059](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0059-i4-check-limpo-compila.md)).

If you want the conversion, it is written: there is no "the compiler sorts it out".

sections.title: I3 — Observable determinism
sections.text:
### I3 — Observable determinism

Same input + same flags ⇒ **same bytes** of output and of diagnostics. This holds for
stdout, stderr, exit code and `--dump-ast`. The following are forbidden in the output: memory
address, PID, timestamp, absolute path, `set`/`dict` order, locale and directory order.

The 1.0 prelude does not read the clock or other ambient inputs: `clock` was removed
([ADR-0026](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0026-freeze-1.0.md)). The **ambient functions** declared in
[ADR-0072](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0072-stdlib-batteries.md) §5 — `args`, `os.getenv`, `time.now`,
`time.sleep`, `std.fs`, `std.io` reads, `std.proc`/`process.*` and kernel
file opening — are explicitly **outside** this guarantee and the differential corpus; they
have their own test with fixed input. `std.fs.listDir` sorts entries by byte precisely so as

buffer (block on a pipe, line on a tty) — as in the oracle. Without the flush, a process that

overflow behavior by design; the guarantee holds for the same flags.

```bash
./lox program.lx > a.txt 2>&1   # twice, on different machines/flags
./lox program.lx > b.txt 2>&1
cmp a.txt b.txt                   # identical
```

The wording of an error message **may change between versions**; the exit code does not
(`65` compilation, `70` runtime). Diagnostic **codes** are stable and never

sections.text:
### I4 — Clean `--check` ⇒ it compiles

Every program that passes `--check` compiles. The **only** acceptable refusal in lowering is the
gap already declared and classified:

```
... is not supported by the backend yet.
```

Any other error after a clean check is an I4 violation. The checker is the **source of
truth** for types; the backend consumes the published types and does not invent its own rule.

```bash
uv run main.py --check prog.lx      # exit 0 …
uv run main.py --emit=exe prog.lx   # … so this compiles (or refuses only "not supported")
```

It is the operational corollary of I1: without it, the same program could give `2` in the
interpreter and a type error in the compiler, with the user receiving two contradictory
diagnostics ([ADR-0059](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0059-i4-check-limpo-compila.md)).

sections.title: Design principles
sections.text:
## Design principles

They are not testable guarantees like I1–I4: they are the criteria that guide syntax, type
and stdlib decisions. What is still aspirational is marked.

1. **No noise** — optional `;`, `elif`, one-line body; the syntax should not require
   ceremony for the common case.
2. **Expressions first** — almost everything produces a value; `if`/`match`/block as an
   expression stayed **outside 1.0** ([ADR-0026](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0026-freeze-1.0.md)); ternary and `??` cover the
   common case.
3. **Immutable by default** — `val`/`var` implemented; parameters are immutable and `var x`
   unlocks mutation. Arguments in [ADR-0005](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0005-val-var-imutabilidade.md).
4. **Optional types, not ceremony** — annotate only where it helps; in `--check` local
   inference already exists and parameters/return remain signed. Inferring a parameter without
   an annotation was postponed; see [ADR-0020](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0020-assinaturas-explicitas.md).
5. **Fail early and clearly** — spans, caret and stack trace exist today
   ([ADR-0075](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0075-diagnosticos-estruturados.md),
   [ADR-0089](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0089-stack-trace-de-runtime.md)).
6. **Predictable** — no implicit coercion, no `nil` surprise; that is I2.
7. **Identity = invariants, not features** — the contract is
   [ADR-0014](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0014-identidade-e-invariantes.md); every feature goes through the admission
   gate.

sections.title: How this is verified
sections.text:
## How this is verified

- [`tests/test_determinism.py`](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/tests/test_determinism.py) runs cases with
  different `PYTHONHASHSEED` and requires byte-for-byte equality (I3), besides forbidding
  volatile data.
- [`tests/test_backend.py`](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/tests/test_backend.py) compiles each manifest case and
  compares stdout/stderr/exit with the interpreter (I1), sweeps the corpus requiring that a
  clean check never becomes a type error (I4) and documents the memory budget.
- The golden cases in `tests/cases/` pin down the I2 refusals (mixed coercion, `nil`
  surprise, division by zero, promotion in storage).
- `tests/test_docs_consistency.py` prevents this page from falling behind the
  manifest and the CLI.

sections.title: What is **not** promised
sections.text:
## What is **not** promised

- **Speed.** The tree-walk is the oracle, not the final product; benchmarks serve to
  detect regression, not to compete with Rust.
- **Message wording between versions.** Only the exit code (and, in the future, the diagnostic
  code) is stable.
- **Compatibility with book Lox.** The language diverged on purpose
  (`val`/`var`, `Int`/`Float`, `class B(A)`); there is no compatibility mode.
- **ABI, bytecode or object format stability.** They do not exist yet, and when they
  exist they will not be a public contract in the first version.
- **Timing.** Nothing promises when a `nil`/object is freed, nor finalization order —
  precisely so as not to break I1.
- **Native-only capabilities under `run`/REPL.** They are refused at compile time
  (`E3021`); there is no interpreted fallback and no promise that the interpreter can run
  every program ([ADR-0128](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0128-contrato-de-motores.md)).
- **Programs above the memory budget** in the binary (default hard cap of 512 MiB and
  I1 up to 64 MiB of live memory) and **above 10,000 Lox calls** (R1015 is the limit).

sections.title: Revisit
sections.text:
## Revisit

If a guarantee turns out to be impossible for a feature, that is **not** resolved by
loosening the text silently: a new ADR says what stops applying and why
(see [ADR-0014](https://github.com/loxia-lang/loxia/blob/main/docs/adr/0014-identidade-e-invariantes.md), "How to verify").

pages.summary: Reference generated from /// in std/*.lx and the builtins registry.

sections.title: Modules
sections.text:
## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| [`std.asserts`](https://loxia-lang.github.io/loxia/stdlib/asserts/) | Explicit failures for tests and contracts. Every helper raises `RuntimeError`. |
| [`std.bytes`](https://loxia-lang.github.io/loxia/stdlib/bytes/) | Byte buffers: incremental Builder, comparison and big/little-endian helpers. |
| [`std.cli`](https://loxia-lang.github.io/loxia/stdlib/cli/) | Deterministic command-line parsing from a declarative spec. |
| [`std.collections`](https://loxia-lang.github.io/loxia/stdlib/collections/) | Stack, Queue, Deque and PriorityQueue, backed by lists. |
| [`std.contracts`](https://loxia-lang.github.io/loxia/stdlib/contracts/) | Design by contract as a library: precondition, postcondition and invariant checks. |
| [`std.convert`](https://loxia-lang.github.io/loxia/stdlib/convert/) | Text conversions (integer/float/bool, Base64, hex) over UTF-8 bytes. |
| [`std.csv`](https://loxia-lang.github.io/loxia/stdlib/csv/) | RFC 4180 CSV parsing and serialization, with CRLF output. |
| [`std.documents`](https://loxia-lang.github.io/loxia/stdlib/documents/) | Full-sync document store: opaque URIs, versions and text, without JSON or I/O. |
| [`std.fmt`](https://loxia-lang.github.io/loxia/stdlib/fmt/) | Locale-free formatting helpers (templates, padding, numbers, byte sizes). |
| [`std.framing`](https://loxia-lang.github.io/loxia/stdlib/framing/) | `Content-Length` framing over an injected byte reader; stdin/stdout only at the edge. |
| [`std.fs`](https://loxia-lang.github.io/loxia/stdlib/fs/) | File reading and writing. Ambient: outside the I1 corpus. |
| [`std.hash`](https://loxia-lang.github.io/loxia/stdlib/hash/) | Non-cryptographic hashes (FNV-1a, djb2) over UTF-8 bytes. |
| [`std.io`](https://loxia-lang.github.io/loxia/stdlib/io/) | Standard input/output. The read functions are ambient where they block. |
| [`std.iter`](https://loxia-lang.github.io/loxia/stdlib/iter/) | Iteration helpers (`enumerate`, `zip`, `sum`, `contains`, `Step`). |
| [`std.json`](https://loxia-lang.github.io/loxia/stdlib/json/) | RFC 8259 JSON with insertion-ordered objects and a 16-level nesting cap. |
| [`std.jsonrpc`](https://loxia-lang.github.io/loxia/stdlib/jsonrpc/) | JSON-RPC 2.0 envelopes: validation, construction, error codes and `Map` messages. |
| [`std.lists`](https://loxia-lang.github.io/loxia/stdlib/lists/) | Generic list combinators; every function leaves the input unchanged. |
| [`std.log`](https://loxia-lang.github.io/loxia/stdlib/log/) | Leveled logging to stderr, without timestamps. |
| [`std.maps`](https://loxia-lang.github.io/loxia/stdlib/maps/) | Helpers for `Map[String, V]` that preserve insertion order. |
| [`std.numeric`](https://loxia-lang.github.io/loxia/stdlib/numeric/) | Integer number theory and population statistics. |
| [`std.paths`](https://loxia-lang.github.io/loxia/stdlib/paths/) | Lexical POSIX path helpers; no filesystem access. |
| [`std.proc`](https://loxia-lang.github.io/loxia/stdlib/proc/) | Processes, streams and `poll` (POSIX, ambient: outside I1/I3). |
| [`std.property`](https://loxia-lang.github.io/loxia/stdlib/property/) | Deterministic property-based testing with generators, shrinking and seeds. |
| [`std.rand`](https://loxia-lang.github.io/loxia/stdlib/rand/) | Deterministic xorshift64* PRNG with an explicit seed. |
| [`std.results`](https://loxia-lang.github.io/loxia/stdlib/results/) | Combinators for `Result[T, E]`. |
| [`std.sets`](https://loxia-lang.github.io/loxia/stdlib/sets/) | `Set[T]` backed by `Map[Any, Bool]`, preserving insertion order. |
| [`std.strings`](https://loxia-lang.github.io/loxia/stdlib/strings/) | UTF-8 text operations over code points, not bytes or UTF-16 units. |
| [`std.test`](https://loxia-lang.github.io/loxia/stdlib/test/) | Mini test harness with TAP output, hooks, matchers and a recorder. |
| [`std.timex`](https://loxia-lang.github.io/loxia/stdlib/timex/) | UTC date/time helpers over integer epoch milliseconds; no timezones. |
| [`std.utf8`](https://loxia-lang.github.io/loxia/stdlib/utf8/) | UTF-8 and UTF-16 widths (bytes, code units, columns). |

sections.title: Functions
sections.text:
## Functions

### `fn assert(condition: Bool, message: String = ...) -> Nil`

Raises `RuntimeError` with `message` when `condition` is false.

Intended for preconditions and invariants; on success it returns `nil` and has no
other effect.

### `fn assertEq[T](actual: T, expected: T, message: String = ...) -> Nil`

Raises `RuntimeError` when the two values differ.

Uses `!=`, so lists, maps and tuples compare structurally. The message includes
both values rendered with `str`, which keeps the failure readable in TAP output.

### `fn assertNotNil[T](value: T | Nil, message: String = ...) -> T`

Returns `value` narrowed to a non-nil type, or raises `RuntimeError`.

The return type removes the optional, so callers can keep using the value without a
second nil check. The default message is `expected a non-nil value`.

### `fn fail(message: String) -> Nil`

Raises `RuntimeError` with `message` unconditionally.

Useful for unreachable branches and for aborting a contract check with a
caller-provided message.
