sections.title: Global functions
sections.text:
## Global functions

### `args() -> List[String]`

Returns the program arguments.

The list excludes the program name (`argv[0]`) and contains the remaining arguments as strings, in command-line order. Ambient: it depends on how the process was launched.

### `chars(s: String) -> List[String]`

Splits a string into its Unicode code points.

Each element is a one-code-point `String`; `chars("")` is `[]`. Indices count code points, not UTF-8 bytes or UTF-16 units. A non-string argument raises `RuntimeError`.

### `charCodeAt(s: String, index: Int) -> Int`

Returns the Unicode code point at a code-point index.

`index` must be in `0..len(s)-1`; anything else raises `RuntimeError`. Astral code points (above U+FFFF) are returned as a single scalar, not as a surrogate pair.

### `fromCodePoint(codePoint: Int) -> String`

Builds a one-code-point string from a Unicode scalar.

Accepts `0..U+10FFFF` except the surrogate range `U+D800..U+DFFF`; invalid values raise `RuntimeError`.

### `join(parts: List[String], separator: String) -> String`

Joins a list of strings with a separator between elements.

Every element must be a `String`, otherwise `RuntimeError` is raised. `join([], ",")` is `""`; no separator is added at either end.

### `len(value: Any) -> Int`

Returns the length of a string, list, map or tuple.

Strings count code points (not bytes); maps count entries; tuples count positions. Any other value raises `RuntimeError`.

### `range(start: Int, end: Int, step: Int) -> Range`

Creates a lazy integer range from `start` to `end` with an explicit step.

`start`, `end` and `step` must be `Int`; `step` can be negative to iterate downwards but cannot be zero. Ranges are immutable and reusable. The two-argument form is the `start..end` operator, which is sugar for a step of 1; `range(a, b)` with two arguments is not accepted.

### `print(value: Any) -> Nil`

Writes the display form of `value` followed by a newline.

Strings are printed raw (without quotes); list, map, tuple and enum elements use their display forms, with string elements quoted. Returns `nil`.

### `repr(value: Any) -> String`

Returns the debug representation of `value`.

Strings are quoted and escaped (`\\`, `"`, newline, CR, tab and NUL); other values match `str`. Used by tests and diagnostics.

### `str(value: Any) -> String`

Returns the display form of `value`.

Strings are returned unchanged, `nil` is `"nil"`, booleans are `true`/`false`, `Int` is decimal and `Float` uses the canonical short form (`1.0`, not `1`).

### `substr(text: String, start: Int, end: Int) -> String`

Returns the half-open code-point slice `[start, end)`.

Requires `start >= 0`, `end >= start` and `end <= len(text)`; any other bound raises `RuntimeError`. `substr(s, 0, len(s))` returns a copy.

sections.title: Namespaces
sections.text:
## Namespaces

### `Int`

Namespace for integer conversions.

Read-only; the only member is `Int.parse`.

#### `Int.parse(text: String) -> Int?`

Parses a decimal integer.

Accepts an optional `+`/`-` followed by ASCII digits only; whitespace, other bases and values outside the i64 range return `nil`. A non-string argument raises `RuntimeError`.

### `Float`

Namespace for float conversions.

Read-only; the only member is `Float.parse`.

#### `Float.parse(text: String) -> Float?`

Parses a decimal float.

Accepts digits with an optional fraction and exponent (`1`, `-2.5`, `1e3`). Whitespace, `NaN`, infinities and overflow return `nil`. A non-string argument raises `RuntimeError`.

### `math`

Deterministic math namespace.

No locale or host state is consulted. Functions returning `Int` (`floor`, `ceil`, `round`, `trunc`) require a finite value in i64 range and raise `RuntimeError` otherwise.

#### `math.abs(value: Int | Float) -> Int | Float`

Returns the absolute value, preserving the argument type.

An `Int` stays `Int` (under `--debug`, `abs(INT_MIN)` raises on overflow); a `Float` stays `Float`.

#### `math.min(a: Int | Float, b: Int | Float) -> Int | Float`

Returns the smaller of two numbers.

Promotes to `Float` when either argument is `Float`; any `NaN` argument makes the result `NaN`.

#### `math.max(a: Int | Float, b: Int | Float) -> Int | Float`

Returns the larger of two numbers.

Promotes to `Float` when either argument is `Float`; any `NaN` argument makes the result `NaN`.

#### `math.clamp(value: Int | Float, low: Int | Float, high: Int | Float) -> Int | Float`

Clamps `value` into the inclusive range `[low, high]`.

Requires `low <= high`; otherwise `RuntimeError` is raised. A `NaN` in any argument makes the result `NaN`; mixed `Int`/`Float` promotes to `Float`.

#### `math.floor(value: Float) -> Int`

Rounds down to an integer.

Requires a `Float`; the value must be finite and fit in i64, otherwise `RuntimeError` is raised.

#### `math.ceil(value: Float) -> Int`

Rounds up to an integer.

Requires a `Float`; the value must be finite and fit in i64, otherwise `RuntimeError` is raised.

#### `math.round(value: Float) -> Int`

Rounds to the nearest integer, with ties away from zero.

Requires a `Float`; the value must be finite and fit in i64, otherwise `RuntimeError` is raised.

#### `math.trunc(value: Float) -> Int`

Truncates toward zero.

Requires a `Float`; the value must be finite and fit in i64, otherwise `RuntimeError` is raised.

#### `math.sqrt(value: Float) -> Float`

Returns the square root as a `Float`.

Requires a `Float`. A negative argument returns `NaN` instead of raising.

### `io`

Standard input/output namespace.

`write`, `writeErr` and `flush` are deterministic; the read functions are ambient and may block.

#### `io.readFile(path: String) -> String?`

Reads a UTF-8 file into a string, or `nil` when it cannot be read.

Ambient. Invalid UTF-8 counts as unreadable (`nil`); the content is returned exactly as stored, including any trailing newline.

#### `io.readAll() -> String`

Reads all remaining standard input as text.

Ambient. At immediate end of input it returns `""`; invalid UTF-8 raises `RuntimeError`.

#### `io.write(text: String) -> Nil`

Writes `text` to standard output without a trailing newline.

Flushes immediately, so output order is observable before the next read or process exit.

#### `io.writeErr(text: String) -> Nil`

Writes `text` to standard error without a trailing newline.

Flushes immediately; stderr is not part of the default golden comparison.

#### `io.writeFile(path: String, text: String) -> Bool`

Writes `text` as UTF-8, creating or truncating the file.

Ambient. Returns `true` on success and `false` on a filesystem error; the parent directory must exist.

#### `io.readLine() -> String?`

Reads one line from standard input.

Ambient. A trailing LF or CRLF is removed; `nil` means immediate end of input. Invalid UTF-8 raises `RuntimeError`.

#### `io.readUtf8(n: Int) -> String?`

Reads exactly `n` bytes and decodes them as strict UTF-8.

Ambient. `nil` only at immediate end of input; a short read or invalid UTF-8 raises `RuntimeError`. `n` must be non-negative; `n == 0` returns `""`.

#### `io.flush() -> Nil`

Flushes standard output and standard error.

### `fs`

Filesystem namespace (ambient).

Operations read the host filesystem and are outside the I1 corpus; tests use temporary directories and never print absolute paths.

#### `fs.exists(path: String) -> Bool`

Returns whether `path` exists.

Ambient. True for files, directories and other entries the host can stat.

#### `fs.open(path: String, mode: String) -> Int`

Opens `path` in mode `r`, `w` or `a` and returns a 1-based handle.

Ambient. `w` truncates/creates and `a` creates and appends; failure raises `RuntimeError` with a stable kind prefix (`notFound: ...`).

#### `fs.read(id: Int, n: Int) -> String?`

Reads at most `n` bytes from a file handle, always a complete UTF-8 prefix.

Ambient. `nil` is end of file; invalid UTF-8 or a handle not open for reading raises.

#### `fs.readBytes(id: Int, n: Int) -> Bytes?`

Reads at most `n` raw bytes from a file handle, without UTF-8 validation.

Ambient. `nil` is immediate end of file and `n == 0` is the empty `Bytes`; a handle not open for reading or a negative `n` raises.

#### `fs.write(id: Int, text: String) -> Nil`

Writes all of `text` to a file handle.

Ambient. A handle opened with `r`, a closed handle or a failed write raises.

#### `fs.close(id: Int) -> Nil`

Closes a file handle; closing it again is a no-op.

Ambient. An id that never existed raises.

#### `fs.rename(source: String, target: String) -> Nil`

Renames `source` to `target` with POSIX semantics: atomic and replacing an existing `target`.

Ambient. Failure raises `RuntimeError` with a stable kind prefix (`notFound: ...`); across filesystems the kind is `crossDevice`.

#### `fs.remove(path: String) -> Nil`

Removes a file or symlink.

Ambient. A directory is an `isDirectory` error; failure raises `RuntimeError`.

#### `fs.mkdir(path: String) -> Nil`

Creates one directory level.

Ambient. An existing path is `alreadyExists`; a missing parent is `notFound`.

#### `fs.stat(path: String) -> (Int, Int, Bool)`

Returns `(size, mtimeMs, isDir)` for `path`, following symlinks.

Ambient. `mtimeMs` is floor milliseconds since the epoch; the filesystem may have coarser resolution. Failure raises `RuntimeError`.

#### `fs.listDir(path: String) -> List[String]?`

Returns the entry names of a directory, sorted, or `nil` when unreadable.

Ambient. The sort makes the result deterministic for a given directory; `.` and `..` are not included.

### `process`

Process and stream handles for the kernel (POSIX, ambient).

Handles are opaque, 1-based `Int` ids; `0` is never a valid handle and is returned by `spawn` on failure.

#### `process.spawn(argv: List[String]) -> Int`

Starts a process without a shell.

Ambient. `argv[0]` is the program and the remaining items are its arguments; stdin/stdout/stderr are pipes. Returns a process handle, or `0` when the process cannot start.

#### `process.stdin(handle: Int) -> Int`

Returns the stream handle for a process's standard input.

Ambient. The process handle must be valid.

#### `process.stdout(handle: Int) -> Int`

Returns the stream handle for a process's standard output.

Ambient. The process handle must be valid.

#### `process.stderr(handle: Int) -> Int`

Returns the stream handle for a process's standard error.

Ambient. The process handle must be valid.

#### `process.wait(handle: Int) -> Int`

Waits for a process and returns its exit code.

Ambient. A negative code means the child was terminated by a signal; the status is cached after the first wait.

#### `process.kill(handle: Int) -> Bool`

Sends `SIGKILL` to a process.

Ambient. Returns `false` when the process already exited; records the exit status when it reaps the child.

#### `process.close(handle: Int) -> Nil`

Releases a process or stream handle.

Ambient. Does not kill a running process; after closing, any use of the handle raises `RuntimeError`.

#### `process.read(handle: Int, n: Int) -> String?`

Reads up to `n` bytes from a stream as UTF-8.

Ambient. `nil` at end of stream; an incomplete UTF-8 sequence is buffered for the next call, so a character is never split. `n` must be non-negative.

#### `process.write(handle: Int, text: String) -> Bool`

Writes all of `text` to a stream.

Ambient. Returns `false` when the other side closed the pipe.

#### `process.poll(handles: List[Int], timeoutMs: Int) -> List[Int]`

Returns the handles that are ready.

Ambient. A negative timeout waits forever and `0` is non-blocking; streams are ready when readable or at EOF, processes when they have exited. The result is deduplicated.

### `os`

Operating-system namespace.

#### `os.exit(code: Int) -> Nil`

Flushes both streams and terminates the process with `code`.

`code` must be in `0..255`; anything else raises `RuntimeError`.

#### `os.getenv(name: String) -> String?`

Returns the value of an environment variable, or `nil` when unset.

Ambient: it reads the host environment.

### `time`

Time namespace (ambient).

Functions read the host clock; they are outside the I1/I3 corpus.

#### `time.now() -> Int`

Returns the current Unix time in milliseconds.

Ambient and non-deterministic; tests must not assert an exact value.

#### `time.sleep(milliseconds: Int) -> Nil`

Suspends the current process for at least `milliseconds`.

Ambient. A negative duration raises `RuntimeError`.

### `Bytes`

Immutable sequence of bytes (0..255).

`len(b)` counts bytes; `b[i]` is an `Int` 0..255; `str`/`repr` render `0x<hex>`; equality is structural and `b == s` is `false`. `Bytes` is not a `Map` key and has no literal syntax. Build with `Bytes.fromText`, `fromList`, `fromHex` or `fromBase64`; slice/concat and conversions are value methods.

#### `Bytes.empty() -> Bytes`

Returns the empty `Bytes`.

#### `Bytes.fromList(xs: List[Int]) -> Bytes`

Copies a list of integers 0..255 into `Bytes`.

A value outside 0..255 (or a non-integer element) raises `RuntimeError`.

#### `Bytes.fromText(text: String) -> Bytes`

Encodes the UTF-8 bytes of `text`.

#### `Bytes.fromHex(text: String) -> Result[Bytes, BytesError]`

Decodes RFC 4648 base16.

Accepts lowercase and uppercase digits; an odd length or a non-hex character is `Err(BytesError.InvalidHex(message))`.

#### `Bytes.fromBase64(text: String) -> Result[Bytes, BytesError]`

Decodes canonical RFC 4648 base64 (standard alphabet, padding required).

Invalid, unpadded or non-canonical input is `Err(BytesError.InvalidBase64(message))`.

#### `Bytes.slice(start: Int, end: Int) -> Bytes`

Returns the half-open byte range `start..end`.

Same bounds rules as `substr`: negative, inverted or past-the-end ranges raise `RuntimeError`.

#### `Bytes.concat(other: Bytes) -> Bytes`

Returns a new `Bytes` with `other` appended; neither operand is mutated.

#### `Bytes.toList() -> List[Int]`

Copies the bytes into a new `List[Int]`.

#### `Bytes.toText() -> Result[String, BytesError]`

Decodes strict UTF-8; invalid input is `Err(BytesError.InvalidUtf8(message))` and is never replaced.

#### `Bytes.toHex() -> String`

Returns lowercase RFC 4648 base16.

#### `Bytes.toBase64() -> String`

Returns canonical RFC 4648 base64 with padding.

sections.text:
### `io`

Standard input/output namespace.

`write`, `writeErr` and `flush` are deterministic; the read functions are ambient and may block.

#### `io.readFile(path: String) -> String?`

Reads a UTF-8 file into a string, or `nil` when it cannot be read.

Ambient. Invalid UTF-8 counts as unreadable (`nil`); the content is returned exactly as stored, including any trailing newline.

#### `io.readAll() -> String`

Reads all remaining standard input as text.

Ambient. At immediate end of input it returns `""`; invalid UTF-8 raises `RuntimeError`.

#### `io.write(text: String) -> Nil`

Writes `text` to standard output without a trailing newline.

Flushes immediately, so output order is observable before the next read or process exit.

#### `io.writeErr(text: String) -> Nil`

Writes `text` to standard error without a trailing newline.

Flushes immediately; stderr is not part of the default golden comparison.

#### `io.writeFile(path: String, text: String) -> Bool`

Writes `text` as UTF-8, creating or truncating the file.

Ambient. Returns `true` on success and `false` on a filesystem error; the parent directory must exist.

#### `io.readLine() -> String?`

Reads one line from standard input.

Ambient. A trailing LF or CRLF is removed; `nil` means immediate end of input. Invalid UTF-8 raises `RuntimeError`.

#### `io.readUtf8(n: Int) -> String?`

Reads exactly `n` bytes and decodes them as strict UTF-8.

Ambient. `nil` only at immediate end of input; a short read or invalid UTF-8 raises `RuntimeError`. `n` must be non-negative; `n == 0` returns `""`.

#### `io.flush() -> Nil`

Flushes standard output and standard error.

sections.title: fs
sections.text:
### `fs`

Filesystem namespace (ambient).

Operations read the host filesystem and are outside the I1 corpus; tests use temporary directories and never print absolute paths.

#### `fs.exists(path: String) -> Bool`

Returns whether `path` exists.

Ambient. True for files, directories and other entries the host can stat.

#### `fs.open(path: String, mode: String) -> Int`

Opens `path` in mode `r`, `w` or `a` and returns a 1-based handle.

Ambient. `w` truncates/creates and `a` creates and appends; failure raises `RuntimeError` with a stable kind prefix (`notFound: ...`).

#### `fs.read(id: Int, n: Int) -> String?`

Reads at most `n` bytes from a file handle, always a complete UTF-8 prefix.

Ambient. `nil` is end of file; invalid UTF-8 or a handle not open for reading raises.

#### `fs.readBytes(id: Int, n: Int) -> Bytes?`

Reads at most `n` raw bytes from a file handle, without UTF-8 validation.

Ambient. `nil` is immediate end of file and `n == 0` is the empty `Bytes`; a handle not open for reading or a negative `n` raises.

#### `fs.write(id: Int, text: String) -> Nil`

Writes all of `text` to a file handle.

Ambient. A handle opened with `r`, a closed handle or a failed write raises.

#### `fs.close(id: Int) -> Nil`

Closes a file handle; closing it again is a no-op.

Ambient. An id that never existed raises.

#### `fs.rename(source: String, target: String) -> Nil`

Renames `source` to `target` with POSIX semantics: atomic and replacing an existing `target`.

Ambient. Failure raises `RuntimeError` with a stable kind prefix (`notFound: ...`); across filesystems the kind is `crossDevice`.

#### `fs.remove(path: String) -> Nil`

Removes a file or symlink.

Ambient. A directory is an `isDirectory` error; failure raises `RuntimeError`.

#### `fs.mkdir(path: String) -> Nil`

Creates one directory level.

Ambient. An existing path is `alreadyExists`; a missing parent is `notFound`.

#### `fs.stat(path: String) -> (Int, Int, Bool)`

Returns `(size, mtimeMs, isDir)` for `path`, following symlinks.

Ambient. `mtimeMs` is floor milliseconds since the epoch; the filesystem may have coarser resolution. Failure raises `RuntimeError`.

#### `fs.listDir(path: String) -> List[String]?`

Returns the entry names of a directory, sorted, or `nil` when unreadable.

Ambient. The sort makes the result deterministic for a given directory; `.` and `..` are not included.

sections.title: process
sections.text:
### `process`

Process and stream handles for the kernel (POSIX, ambient).

Handles are opaque, 1-based `Int` ids; `0` is never a valid handle and is returned by `spawn` on failure.

#### `process.spawn(argv: List[String]) -> Int`

Starts a process without a shell.

Ambient. `argv[0]` is the program and the remaining items are its arguments; stdin/stdout/stderr are pipes. Returns a process handle, or `0` when the process cannot start.

#### `process.stdin(handle: Int) -> Int`

Returns the stream handle for a process's standard input.

Ambient. The process handle must be valid.

#### `process.stdout(handle: Int) -> Int`

Returns the stream handle for a process's standard output.

Ambient. The process handle must be valid.

#### `process.stderr(handle: Int) -> Int`

Returns the stream handle for a process's standard error.

Ambient. The process handle must be valid.

#### `process.wait(handle: Int) -> Int`

Waits for a process and returns its exit code.

Ambient. A negative code means the child was terminated by a signal; the status is cached after the first wait.

#### `process.kill(handle: Int) -> Bool`

Sends `SIGKILL` to a process.

Ambient. Returns `false` when the process already exited; records the exit status when it reaps the child.

#### `process.close(handle: Int) -> Nil`

Releases a process or stream handle.

Ambient. Does not kill a running process; after closing, any use of the handle raises `RuntimeError`.

#### `process.read(handle: Int, n: Int) -> String?`

Reads up to `n` bytes from a stream as UTF-8.

Ambient. `nil` at end of stream; an incomplete UTF-8 sequence is buffered for the next call, so a character is never split. `n` must be non-negative.

#### `process.write(handle: Int, text: String) -> Bool`

Writes all of `text` to a stream.

Ambient. Returns `false` when the other side closed the pipe.

#### `process.poll(handles: List[Int], timeoutMs: Int) -> List[Int]`

Returns the handles that are ready.

Ambient. A negative timeout waits forever and `0` is non-blocking; streams are ready when readable or at EOF, processes when they have exited. The result is deduplicated.

Operating-system namespace.

#### `os.exit(code: Int) -> Nil`

Flushes both streams and terminates the process with `code`.

`code` must be in `0..255`; anything else raises `RuntimeError`.

### `time`

Time namespace (ambient).

Functions read the host clock; they are outside the I1/I3 corpus.

#### `time.now() -> Int`

Returns the current Unix time in milliseconds.

Ambient and non-deterministic; tests must not assert an exact value.

#### `time.sleep(milliseconds: Int) -> Nil`

Suspends the current process for at least `milliseconds`.

Ambient. A negative duration raises `RuntimeError`.

sections.title: Bytes
sections.text:
### `Bytes`

Immutable sequence of bytes (0..255).

`len(b)` counts bytes; `b[i]` is an `Int` 0..255; `str`/`repr` render `0x<hex>`; equality is structural and `b == s` is `false`. `Bytes` is not a `Map` key and has no literal syntax. Build with `Bytes.fromText`, `fromList`, `fromHex` or `fromBase64`; slice/concat and conversions are value methods.

#### `Bytes.empty() -> Bytes`

Returns the empty `Bytes`.

#### `Bytes.fromList(xs: List[Int]) -> Bytes`

Copies a list of integers 0..255 into `Bytes`.

A value outside 0..255 (or a non-integer element) raises `RuntimeError`.

#### `Bytes.fromText(text: String) -> Bytes`

Encodes the UTF-8 bytes of `text`.

#### `Bytes.fromHex(text: String) -> Result[Bytes, BytesError]`

Decodes RFC 4648 base16.

Accepts lowercase and uppercase digits; an odd length or a non-hex character is `Err(BytesError.InvalidHex(message))`.

#### `Bytes.fromBase64(text: String) -> Result[Bytes, BytesError]`

Decodes canonical RFC 4648 base64 (standard alphabet, padding required).

Invalid, unpadded or non-canonical input is `Err(BytesError.InvalidBase64(message))`.

#### `Bytes.slice(start: Int, end: Int) -> Bytes`

Returns the half-open byte range `start..end`.

Same bounds rules as `substr`: negative, inverted or past-the-end ranges raise `RuntimeError`.

#### `Bytes.concat(other: Bytes) -> Bytes`

Returns a new `Bytes` with `other` appended; neither operand is mutated.

#### `Bytes.toList() -> List[Int]`

Copies the bytes into a new `List[Int]`.

#### `Bytes.toText() -> Result[String, BytesError]`

Decodes strict UTF-8; invalid input is `Err(BytesError.InvalidUtf8(message))` and is never replaced.

#### `Bytes.toHex() -> String`

Returns lowercase RFC 4648 base16.

#### `Bytes.toBase64() -> String`

Returns canonical RFC 4648 base64 with padding.

sections.title: Built-in types
sections.text:
## Built-in types

### `Result[T, E]`

Built-in generic sum type with `Result.Ok(value)` and `Result.Err(error)`.

Use an exhaustive `match` to inspect it, or the combinators in `std.results`.

### `BytesError`

Failure of a `Bytes` conversion.

Variants: `BytesError.InvalidHex(message)`, `InvalidBase64(message)` and `InvalidUtf8(message)`. Available without an import; use `match` to inspect it.

### `Exception`

Base class for catchable runtime errors.

`except Exception as e` catches user exceptions and runtime panics converted to `RuntimeError`.

### `RuntimeError`

Catchable runtime error type, below `Exception`.

Raised by the `raise` statement and by runtime panics; the `message` field holds the diagnostic text.

sections.title: Classes

## Classes

### `class Builder`

Acumula bytes e materializa um `Bytes` no fim.

#### `fn init()`

Cria um Builder vazio.

#### `fn push(data: Bytes) -> Builder`

Anexa todos os bytes de `data` e devolve o próprio Builder.

#### `fn pushByte(value: Int) -> Builder`

Anexa um único byte 0..255 e devolve o próprio Builder.

#### `fn len() -> Int`

Número de bytes acumulados.

#### `fn build() -> Bytes`

Materializa uma cópia imutável; o Builder continua utilizável.

### `class ChunkBuilder`

Acumula blocos `Bytes` e materializa um `Bytes` por concatenação balanceada.

Para montar byte a byte use `Builder`; este evita a `List[Int]` e é indicado para
blocos grandes. O `build` copia O(n log k) no total (k = número de blocos), sem
manter uma cópia intermediária de todos os bytes; um único bloco é devolvido como
está (Bytes é imutável).

#### `fn init()`

Cria um ChunkBuilder vazio.

#### `fn push(data: Bytes) -> ChunkBuilder`

Anexa um bloco (blocos vazios são ignorados) e devolve o próprio builder.

#### `fn len() -> Int`

Número total de bytes acumulados.

#### `fn build() -> Bytes`

Materializa os blocos; o builder continua utilizável.

manter uma cópia intermediária de todos os bytes; um único bloco é devolvido como
está (Bytes é imutável).

#### `fn init()`

Cria um ChunkBuilder vazio.

#### `fn push(data: Bytes) -> ChunkBuilder`

Anexa um bloco (blocos vazios são ignorados) e devolve o próprio builder.

#### `fn len() -> Int`

Número total de bytes acumulados.

#### `fn build() -> Bytes`

Materializa os blocos; o builder continua utilizável.

## Functions

### `fn compare(left: Bytes, right: Bytes) -> Int`

Compara dois `Bytes` lexicograficamente: -1, 0 ou 1.

### `fn u16be(value: Int) -> Bytes`

Encodes `value` (0..65535) as two big-endian bytes.

### `fn u16le(value: Int) -> Bytes`

Encodes `value` (0..65535) as two little-endian bytes.

### `fn u32be(value: Int) -> Bytes`

Encodes `value` (0..4294967295) as four big-endian bytes.

### `fn u32le(value: Int) -> Bytes`

Encodes `value` (0..4294967295) as four little-endian bytes.

### `fn u64be(value: Int) -> Bytes`

Encodes the 64-bit two's-complement pattern of `value` as eight big-endian bytes.

### `fn u64le(value: Int) -> Bytes`

Encodes the 64-bit two's-complement pattern of `value` as eight little-endian bytes.

### `fn readU16be(data: Bytes, offset: Int) -> Int | Nil`

Reads a big-endian `u16` at `offset`; `nil` if the two bytes are out of bounds.

### `fn readU16le(data: Bytes, offset: Int) -> Int | Nil`

Reads a little-endian `u16` at `offset`; `nil` if the two bytes are out of bounds.

### `fn readU32be(data: Bytes, offset: Int) -> Int | Nil`

Reads a big-endian `u32` at `offset`; `nil` if the four bytes are out of bounds.

### `fn readU32le(data: Bytes, offset: Int) -> Int | Nil`

Reads a little-endian `u32` at `offset`; `nil` if the four bytes are out of bounds.

### `fn readU64be(data: Bytes, offset: Int) -> Int | Nil`

Reads a big-endian `u64` at `offset`; `nil` if the eight bytes are out of bounds.

The result is the 64-bit pattern in an `Int`: a value with the high bit set
appears negative, exactly like `u64be`.

### `fn readU64le(data: Bytes, offset: Int) -> Int | Nil`

Reads a little-endian `u64` at `offset`; `nil` if the eight bytes are out of bounds.

The high bit appears as a negative `Int`, exactly like `u64le`.

pages.title: std.cli
pages.summary: Deterministic command-line parsing from a declarative spec.

sections.title: API
sections.text: ## API

sections.title: Functions
sections.text:
## Functions

### `fn parse(args: List[String], spec: List[String]) -> Map[String, Any]`

Parses command-line arguments against a declarative spec into a map.

`args` is the raw argument list without the program name. `spec` lists
`flag:NAME`, `option:NAME` and `positional:NAME` entries; the result contains one
key per name. Missing flags are `false`, missing options and positionals are `nil`.
Options accept `--name value` and `--name=value`, and `--` switches to
positional-only parsing.

Raises `RuntimeError` for an invalid or duplicate spec entry, an unknown option, a
missing option value, or a positional argument that the spec does not declare.

### `fn flag(parsed: Map[String, Any], name: String) -> Bool`

Returns whether a boolean flag was present.

Returns `false` when `name` is absent or does not hold a `Bool`, so a value from a
mismatched spec never raises.

### `fn option(parsed: Map[String, Any], name: String) -> String | Nil`

Returns the value of an option, or `nil` when absent.

Also returns `nil` when `name` is absent or does not hold a `String`.

### `fn positional(parsed: Map[String, Any], name: String) -> String | Nil`

Returns a positional argument, or `nil` when absent.

Positionals are stored as `String` values, so this is equivalent to `option`.

### `fn usage(program: String, spec: List[String]) -> String`

Renders a deterministic usage block from the declared spec.

The first line is `Usage: <program> [options] <positional>...`; one detail line per
spec entry follows, using `--name` for flags and `--name <value>` for options.

pages.title: std.collections
pages.summary: Stack, Queue, Deque and PriorityQueue, backed by lists.

sections.title: API
sections.text: ## API

sections.title: Classes
sections.text:
## Classes

### `class Stack[T]`

Generic LIFO stack backed by a list.

#### `var items: List[T]`

Elements from bottom to top.

#### `fn init()`

Creates an empty stack.

#### `fn push(value: T) -> Nil`

Pushes `value` onto the top.

#### `fn pop() -> T | Nil`

Removes and returns the top, or `nil` when the stack is empty.

#### `fn peek() -> T | Nil`

Returns the top without removing it, or `nil` when the stack is empty.

#### `fn len() -> Int`

Returns the number of elements.

#### `fn isEmpty() -> Bool`

Returns `true` when the stack has no elements.

#### `fn toList() -> List[T]`

Returns a copy of the elements from top to bottom.

#### `fn clear() -> Nil`

Removes every element.

### `class Queue[T]`

Generic FIFO queue backed by a list and a moving head index.

#### `var items: List[T]`

Elements in arrival order; slots before `head` are already consumed.

#### `var head: Int`

Index of the next element to dequeue.

#### `fn init()`

Creates an empty queue.

#### `fn enqueue(value: T) -> Nil`

Adds `value` at the back of the queue.

#### `fn dequeue() -> T | Nil`

Removes and returns the oldest element, or `nil` when the queue is empty.

#### `fn peek() -> T | Nil`

Returns the oldest element without removing it, or `nil` when empty.

#### `fn len() -> Int`

Returns the number of live elements; consumed slots are not counted.

#### `fn isEmpty() -> Bool`

Returns `true` when the queue has no elements.

#### `fn toList() -> List[T]`

Returns a copy of the elements in dequeue order.

#### `fn clear() -> Nil`

Removes every element.

### `class Deque[T]`

Generic double-ended queue backed by two lists.

#### `var front: List[T]`

Front half, with the front element at the end of the list.

#### `var back: List[T]`

Back half, with the back element at the end of the list.

#### `fn init()`

Creates an empty deque.

#### `fn pushFront(value: T) -> Nil`

Inserts `value` at the front.

#### `fn pushBack(value: T) -> Nil`

Inserts `value` at the back.

#### `fn popFront() -> T | Nil`

Removes and returns the front element, or `nil` when empty.

#### `fn popBack() -> T | Nil`

Removes and returns the back element, or `nil` when empty.

#### `fn peekFront() -> T | Nil`

Returns the front element without removing it, or `nil` when empty.

#### `fn peekBack() -> T | Nil`

Returns the back element without removing it, or `nil` when empty.

#### `fn len() -> Int`

Returns the number of elements.

#### `fn isEmpty() -> Bool`

Returns `true` when the deque has no elements.

#### `fn toList() -> List[T]`

Returns a copy from front to back.

#### `fn clear() -> Nil`

Removes every element.

### `class PriorityQueue[T]`

Min-priority queue backed by a binary heap and an explicit comparator.

#### `var items: List[T]`

Heap array in partial order.

#### `val less: fn(T, T) -> Bool`

Comparator: returns `true` when `a` must leave before `b`.

#### `fn init(less: fn(T, T) -> Bool)`

Creates an empty queue; `less` defines the priority order.

#### `fn push(value: T) -> Nil`

Inserts `value` and restores the heap order.

#### `fn pop() -> T | Nil`

Removes and returns the highest-priority (least) element, or `nil` when empty.

#### `fn peek() -> T | Nil`

Returns the highest-priority element without removing it, or `nil` when empty.

#### `fn len() -> Int`

Returns the number of elements.

#### `fn isEmpty() -> Bool`

Returns `true` when the priority queue has no elements.

#### `fn toList() -> List[T]`

Returns a copy in priority order without modifying the queue.

#### `fn clear() -> Nil`

Removes every element.

pages.summary: Design by contract as a library: precondition, postcondition and invariant checks.

sections.title: API
sections.text: ## API

sections.title: Classes
sections.text:
## Classes

### `class ContractError(Exception)`

Error raised when a precondition, postcondition or invariant is violated.

It extends `Exception`, not `RuntimeError`: a contract violation is a programming
bug and must be caught explicitly (`except ContractError`) or terminate the program.

#### `fn init(message: String)`

Creates the error with the message shown in the diagnostic.

sections.title: class ContractError(Exception)
sections.text:
### `class ContractError(Exception)`

Error raised when a precondition, postcondition or invariant is violated.

It extends `Exception`, not `RuntimeError`: a contract violation is a programming
bug and must be caught explicitly (`except ContractError`) or terminate the program.

#### `fn init(message: String)`

Creates the error with the message shown in the diagnostic.

sections.title: fn init(message: String)
sections.text:
#### `fn init(message: String)`

Creates the error with the message shown in the diagnostic.

sections.title: Functions
sections.text:
## Functions

### `fn require(condition: Bool, message: String = ...) -> Nil`

Requires `condition`; raises `ContractError(message)` when it is false.

Use it at the top of a function or method. The default message is
`precondition failed`; prefer a message that names the function and the condition.

### `fn ensure(condition: Bool, message: String = ...) -> Nil`

Ensures `condition`; raises `ContractError(message)` when it is false.

Use it after the body computed `result`, before returning. For single-exit functions
prefer `check`, which evaluates the postcondition automatically.

### `fn checkInvariant(condition: Bool, message: String = ...) -> Nil`

Checks an invariant; raises `ContractError(message)` when it is false.

Invariants are cooperative: fields are public, so this checks only the points where
the code calls it (typically the end of `init` and the boundary of public methods).

### `fn check[T](name: String, pre: fn() -> Bool, body: fn() -> T, post: fn(T) -> Bool) -> T`

Runs `body` between `pre` and `post`, returning its result.

`pre` is evaluated before the body; when it is false, the body is not executed.
`post` receives the result and is evaluated only when the body returns normally.
If the body raises, the postcondition is not evaluated.

The `old` value is a local captured before the call; pass a closure that reads it.

### `fn checkMethod[T, R](name: String, self: T, pre: fn(T) -> Bool, body: fn(T) -> R, post: fn(T, R) -> Bool) -> R`

Like `check`, but for a method with an explicit receiver.

The receiver is passed as `self` instead of being captured as `this`; that keeps the
closure independent from the method frame and works in both engines. The predicates
take the receiver as their first parameter.

### `fn checkVoid(name: String, pre: fn() -> Bool, body: fn() -> Nil, post: fn() -> Bool) -> Nil`

Like `check`, but for a function returning `Nil`.

The postcondition takes no result parameter, which reads better for procedures and
avoids the dummy `Nil` argument that `check` would need.

### `fn checkMethodVoid[T](name: String, self: T, pre: fn(T) -> Bool, body: fn(T) -> Nil, post: fn(T) -> Bool) -> Nil`

Like `checkMethod`, but for a method returning `Nil`.

sections.title: fn require(condition: Bool, message: String = ...) -> Nil
sections.text:
### `fn require(condition: Bool, message: String = ...) -> Nil`

Requires `condition`; raises `ContractError(message)` when it is false.

Use it at the top of a function or method. The default message is
`precondition failed`; prefer a message that names the function and the condition.

sections.title: fn ensure(condition: Bool, message: String = ...) -> Nil
sections.text:
### `fn ensure(condition: Bool, message: String = ...) -> Nil`

Ensures `condition`; raises `ContractError(message)` when it is false.

Use it after the body computed `result`, before returning. For single-exit functions
prefer `check`, which evaluates the postcondition automatically.

sections.title: fn checkInvariant(condition: Bool, message: String = ...) -> Nil
sections.text:
### `fn checkInvariant(condition: Bool, message: String = ...) -> Nil`

Checks an invariant; raises `ContractError(message)` when it is false.

Invariants are cooperative: fields are public, so this checks only the points where
the code calls it (typically the end of `init` and the boundary of public methods).

sections.title: fn check[T](name: String, pre: fn() -> Bool, body: fn() -> T, post: fn(T) -> Bool) -> T
sections.text:
### `fn check[T](name: String, pre: fn() -> Bool, body: fn() -> T, post: fn(T) -> Bool) -> T`

Runs `body` between `pre` and `post`, returning its result.

`pre` is evaluated before the body; when it is false, the body is not executed.
`post` receives the result and is evaluated only when the body returns normally.
If the body raises, the postcondition is not evaluated.

The `old` value is a local captured before the call; pass a closure that reads it.

pages.title: std.convert
pages.summary: Text conversions (integer/float/bool, Base64, hex) over UTF-8 bytes.

sections.title: API
sections.text: ## API

sections.title: Functions
sections.text:
## Functions

### `fn toInt(text: String) -> Int | Nil`

Parses a decimal integer, returning `nil` when invalid.

Delegates to `Int.parse`: an optional `+`/`-` followed by ASCII digits, with no
surrounding whitespace. Values outside the i64 range return `nil`.

### `fn toFloat(text: String) -> Float | Nil`

Parses a decimal float, returning `nil` when invalid.

Delegates to `Float.parse`: digits with an optional fraction and exponent
(`1`, `-2.5`, `1e3`). Surrounding whitespace is rejected, and non-finite results
return `nil`.

### `fn toBool(text: String) -> Bool | Nil`

Parses `true` or `false`, returning `nil` when invalid.

The match is exact: `True` and `FALSE` return `nil`, as does any other text.

### `fn base64Encode(text: String) -> String`

Encodes UTF-8 text as standard Base64.

Uses the `A-Z a-z 0-9 + /` alphabet with `=` padding and no line breaks. Each code
point is first expanded to its UTF-8 bytes, so the result depends only on the text.

### `fn base64Decode(text: String) -> String | Nil`

Decodes standard Base64 into UTF-8 text.

Requires padded input whose length is a multiple of 4. Returns `nil` for invalid
characters, misplaced padding, or bytes that are not valid UTF-8. The empty string
decodes to `""`.

### `fn hexEncode(text: String) -> String`

Encodes UTF-8 text as lowercase hexadecimal.

Each UTF-8 byte becomes two lowercase digits, so the result is twice as long as the
byte sequence.

### `fn hexDecode(text: String) -> String | Nil`

Decodes hexadecimal into UTF-8 text.

Accepts lowercase and uppercase digits and requires an even number of them. Returns
`nil` for invalid digits or bytes that are not valid UTF-8.

sections.title: Functions
sections.text:
## Functions

### `fn parse(text: String) -> List[List[String]] | Nil`

Parses RFC 4180 CSV text into rows of fields.

Accepts LF and CRLF line endings and preserves empty fields. Returns `nil` on
malformed input, including a stray quote in an unquoted field or an unterminated
quoted field. Empty text parses to `[]`; a blank line is a record with one empty
field, not an empty row.

### `fn parseResult(text: String) -> Result[List[List[String]], CsvError]`

Parses CSV text, preserving the cause of a malformed input.

Empty text is `Ok([])`; a stray quote or an unterminated quoted field is
`Err(CsvError("invalidCsv", ...))`.

### `fn stringify(rows: List[List[String]]) -> String`

Serializes rows as RFC 4180 CSV, quoting fields when needed.

Fields are quoted when they contain `,`, `"`, CR or LF, and embedded quotes are
doubled. Every row ends with CRLF, including the last one; an empty row raises
`RuntimeError` because RFC 4180 has no representation for it. `[]` yields `""`.

sections.title: API
sections.text: ## API

sections.title: Classes
sections.text:
## Classes

### `class Document`

One open document and its last known version.

#### `val uri: String`

Opaque document identifier, usually a `file://` URI.

#### `val languageId: String`

Editor language id, e.g. `loxia`.

#### `val version: Int`

Monotonically increasing version supplied by the client.

#### `val text: String`

Full text of the document.

#### `fn init(uri: String, languageId: String, version: Int, text: String)`

Creates a document snapshot.

### `class DocumentError`

Why a store operation failed; `kind` is stable and `message` is for humans.

Kinds: `already_open` (opening an open URI), `not_open` (changing/closing an unknown
URI), `stale_version` (change not newer than the stored version), `invalid_version`
(negative version on open).

#### `val kind: String`

Stable machine-readable kind.

#### `val message: String`

Human-readable reason; a fixed message plus the caller-provided URI.

#### `fn init(kind: String, message: String)`

Creates an error with an explicit kind and message.

### `class DocumentStore`

Full-sync store keyed by opaque URI.

`change` replaces the whole text: range-based changes are not representable here and
belong to the adapter that parses the notification. Versions must increase on every
change; a stale version is rejected instead of silently overwriting newer text.

#### `var docs: Map[String, Document]`

Open documents keyed by URI, in insertion order.

#### `fn init()`

Creates an empty store.

#### `fn open(uri: String, languageId: String, version: Int, text: String) -> Result[Bool, DocumentError]`

Registers a document; fails when the URI is already open or the version is negative.

#### `fn change(uri: String, version: Int, text: String) -> Result[Bool, DocumentError]`

Replaces the full text of an open document.

`version` must be strictly greater than the stored one; otherwise the change is
rejected and the stored text is left untouched.

#### `fn close(uri: String) -> Result[Bool, DocumentError]`

Removes an open document; fails when the URI is unknown.

#### `fn get(uri: String) -> Document | Nil`

Returns the document snapshot, or `nil` when the URI is not open.

#### `fn text(uri: String) -> String | Nil`

Returns the current text, or `nil` when the URI is not open.

#### `fn version(uri: String) -> Int | Nil`

Returns the last version, or `nil` when the URI is not open.

#### `fn languageId(uri: String) -> String | Nil`

Returns the language id, or `nil` when the URI is not open.

#### `fn has(uri: String) -> Bool`

Returns `true` when the URI is open.

#### `fn uris() -> List[String]`

Returns the open URIs in ascending order, independent of insertion order.

#### `fn len() -> Int`

Returns the number of open documents.

pages.title: std.fmt
pages.summary: Locale-free formatting helpers (templates, padding, numbers, byte sizes).

sections.title: API
sections.text: ## API

sections.title: Functions
sections.text:
## Functions

### `fn format(template: String, ...values: Any) -> String`

Replaces each `{}` placeholder with the next value rendered by `str`.

`{{` and `}}` produce literal braces. Raises `RuntimeError` for a malformed
placeholder (such as a lone `{` or `}`) or when the number of values does not match
the number of placeholders.

### `fn pad(text: String, width: Int, fill: String = ...) -> String`

Left-pads `text` to `width` using repeated `fill`.

`fill` must be exactly one code point. Text that is already at least `width` long is
returned unchanged. A negative width or a multi-character fill raises `RuntimeError`.

### `fn commas(value: Int) -> String`

Formats an integer with `,` thousands separators.

Negative values keep a leading `-`; the sign itself is never grouped. `commas(0)` is
`"0"` and the output is independent of locale.

### `fn fixed(value: Float, digits: Int) -> String`

Formats a finite `Float` with exactly `digits` decimal places.

Rounds with `math.round` and pads the fraction with zeros. `digits` must be in
0..15 and the value must be finite; otherwise `RuntimeError` is raised. With
`digits == 0` the result has no decimal point.

### `fn percent(value: Float, digits: Int = ...) -> String`

Formats a value as a percentage with `digits` decimal places.

Multiplies by 100, formats with `fixed` and appends `%`, so the same digit and
finiteness rules apply.

### `fn bytes(value: Int) -> String`

Formats a byte count with a binary unit (`B`, `KiB`, `MiB`, `GiB` or `TiB`).

Scales by 1024 and uses one decimal place above `B`. Negative input raises
`RuntimeError`; `bytes(0)` is `"0 B"`.

sections.title: Functions
sections.text:
## Functions

### `fn readFrame(read: Reader) -> Result[String | Nil, FrameFailure]`

Reads one frame, returning its body.

`Result.Ok(nil)` is a clean end of input at a frame boundary. Headers must be ASCII
and end with CRLF; `Content-Length` is required, unique and counts UTF-8 bytes;
`Content-Type` is accepted and ignored. The body is returned as text, still
unparsed; pair with `std.jsonrpc.decode` for JSON-RPC.

### `fn encodeFrame(text: String) -> String`

Serializes one frame: `Content-Length` counts UTF-8 bytes, then the body.

### `fn readStdin(count: Int) -> String | Nil`

Reads from stdin with `io.readUtf8`, the exact-bytes reader.

Ambient: blocks until `count` bytes or end of input. A truncated body is normalized
to `nil` (the codec reports `truncated`); invalid UTF-8 raises `RuntimeError`, which
`readFrame` turns into a `read` failure.

### `fn writeStdout(text: String) -> Nil`

Writes a complete frame to stdout and flushes it.

Ambient. `io.write` flushes on every call (ADR-0094), so a client waiting for the
response never deadlocks. Never use `print` for protocol output.

sections.title: Functions
sections.text:
## Functions

### `fn open(path: String, mode: String) -> Result[File, FileError]`

Opens `path` in mode `r`, `w` or `a`.

`w` truncates/creates, `a` creates and appends; `r` requires the file to exist.

### `fn withOpen[T](path: String, mode: String, body: fn(File) -> T) -> Result[T, FileError]`

Opens `path`, calls `body` and closes the file even when `body` raises.

This is the scoped form of `open`, replacing a `with` block: the handle never
escapes, and the close runs on normal return and on error.

### `fn readText(path: String) -> Result[String, FileError]`

Reads a UTF-8 file into a string.

### `fn readLines(path: String) -> Result[List[String], FileError]`

Reads a UTF-8 file as one string per line (LF and CRLF; no trailing empty item).

### `fn writeText(path: String, text: String) -> Result[Nil, FileError]`

Writes `text` as UTF-8, overwriting/creating the file.

### `fn appendText(path: String, text: String) -> Result[Nil, FileError]`

Appends `text` as UTF-8, creating the file when missing.

### `fn exists(path: String) -> Bool`

Returns whether `path` exists (file, directory or other entry).

### `fn listDir(path: String) -> Result[List[String], FileError]`

Lists directory entry names in sorted order.

### `fn stat(path: String) -> Result[FileStat, FileError]`

Returns metadata for `path`, following symlinks.

### `fn rename(source: String, target: String) -> Result[Nil, FileError]`

Renames `source` to `target`, replacing an existing target (POSIX `rename`).

### `fn remove(path: String) -> Result[Nil, FileError]`

Removes a file or symlink; a directory is an `isDirectory` error.

### `fn mkdir(path: String) -> Result[Nil, FileError]`

Creates one directory level; an existing path is `Err(alreadyExists)`.

### `fn mkdirAll(path: String) -> Result[Nil, FileError]`

Creates `path` and any missing parents.

Idempotent for an existing directory. Lexical POSIX paths; no symlink resolution.

### `fn writeAtomic(path: String, text: String, suffix: String = ...) -> Result[Nil, FileError]`

Writes `text` to `path` through a temporary file and a rename.

The temporary is `path + suffix`, or `path + suffix + N` when taken (up to 100
attempts), so concurrent writers are unlikely to collide; the destination is
replaced atomically. There is no `fsync`: this is atomicity, not durability.

pages.title: std.hash
pages.summary: Non-cryptographic hashes (FNV-1a, djb2) over UTF-8 bytes.

sections.title: API
sections.text: ## API

sections.title: Functions
sections.text:
## Functions

### `fn fnv1a32(text: String) -> Int`

Returns the 32-bit FNV-1a hash of the UTF-8 bytes of `text`.

The result is masked to 0..4294967295, so it is never negative.

### `fn fnv1a64(text: String) -> Int`

Returns the 64-bit FNV-1a hash of the UTF-8 bytes of `text`.

The result is the i64 bit pattern and may be negative; compare it as an `Int`, not
as an unsigned value.

### `fn djb2(text: String) -> Int`

Returns the 32-bit djb2 hash of the UTF-8 bytes of `text`.

The result is masked to 0..4294967295, so it is never negative.

### `fn sha256(text: String) -> String`

Returns the SHA-256 of the UTF-8 bytes of `text` as 64 lowercase hex characters.

A cryptographic digest (FIPS 180-4) for integrity and content addressing, computed
by the kernel primitive `digest.sha256`; deterministic in both engines. It is not a
password hash — use a dedicated KDF for secrets.

### `fn sha256Bytes(data: Bytes) -> Bytes`

Returns the raw 32-byte SHA-256 of `data`.

The binary counterpart of `sha256`; use `toHex` when a printable digest is needed.

## Functions

### `fn write(text: String) -> Nil`

Writes `text` to stdout without a trailing newline.

Flushes immediately, so the text is visible before the next read or process exit.

### `fn writeErr(text: String) -> Nil`

Writes `text` to stderr without a trailing newline.

Flushes immediately; deterministic, but stderr is not part of the default golden
comparison.

### `fn readLine() -> String | Nil`

Reads one line from stdin, returning `nil` at end of input.

Ambient. A trailing LF or CRLF is removed. Invalid UTF-8 raises instead of returning
a replacement character.

### `fn readAll() -> String`

Reads all remaining stdin as text.

Ambient. At end of input an empty string is returned. Invalid UTF-8 raises.

### `fn prompt(message: String) -> String | Nil`

Writes `message` and reads one line from stdin.

Ambient. The message is written without a trailing newline, then `readLine` is
called; `nil` means end of input.

### `fn enumerate[T](items: List[T]) -> List[(Int, T)]`

Returns `(index, element)` pairs in list order.

Indices start at 0 and match the positions in the input; the result has the same
length as `items`.

### `fn zip[A, B](left: List[A], right: List[B]) -> List[(A, B)]`

Pairs elements from `left` and `right`, stopping at the shorter list.

Uses `==`, so lists, maps and tuples compare structurally.

### `fn any[T](items: List[T], predicate: fn(T) -> Bool) -> Bool`

Stops at the first match. An empty list returns `false`.

### `fn all[T](items: List[T], predicate: fn(T) -> Bool) -> Bool`

Returns whether every element satisfies `predicate`.

Stops at the first mismatch. An empty list satisfies it vacuously.

### `fn find[T](items: List[T], predicate: fn(T) -> Bool) -> T | Nil`

Returns the first element that satisfies `predicate`, or `nil` when none matches.

sections.title: Functions
sections.text:
## Functions

### `fn parse(text: String) -> Any`

Parses RFC 8259 JSON text into Loxia values.

Accepts `null`, booleans, numbers, strings, arrays and objects. A number without a
fraction or exponent stays `Int` when it fits, otherwise it becomes `Float`;
non-finite values are rejected. Objects preserve key order and a repeated key keeps
the last value. Invalid input (bad escapes, trailing characters, nesting deeper than
16) returns `nil`; a valid JSON `null` also returns `nil`. Use `parseResult` when the
caller must distinguish malformed text from a valid `null`.

### `fn parseResult(text: String) -> JsonResult`

Parses JSON text, preserving the difference between `null` and invalid text.

Returns `JsonResult.Ok(nil)` for the JSON literal `null` and `JsonResult.Err(message)`
for malformed input, including the 16-level nesting cap. The message is the same one
`parse` used to hide and never contains a path, timestamp or address.

### `fn isOk(result: JsonResult) -> Bool`

Returns `true` when `result` came from a valid JSON text.

Exists because an enum type exported by a module cannot be named in another module's
annotations; callers use these helpers instead of writing a typed wrapper function.

### `fn value(result: JsonResult) -> Any`

Returns the parsed value, or `nil` when the text was invalid.

### `fn error(result: JsonResult) -> String | Nil`

Returns the error message, or `nil` when the text was valid.

### `fn stringify(value: Any) -> String`

Serializes a Loxia value as compact JSON.

Supports `nil`, `Bool`, `Int`, `Float`, `String`, `List[Any]` and
`Map[String, Any]`. `Int` is emitted without a decimal point and `Float` with one;
a non-finite float raises `RuntimeError`. Object keys keep insertion order, and any
other type raises `RuntimeError`.

### `fn pretty(value: Any, indent: Int = ...) -> String`

Serializes a Loxia value as indented JSON.

Uses `indent` spaces per nesting level and the same value rules as `stringify`.
`indent <= 0` falls back to compact output. Non-empty containers are always broken
across lines; empty ones render as `[]` or `{}`.

sections.title: fn parse(text: String) -> Any
sections.text:
### `fn parse(text: String) -> Any`

Parses RFC 8259 JSON text into Loxia values.

Accepts `null`, booleans, numbers, strings, arrays and objects. A number without a
fraction or exponent stays `Int` when it fits, otherwise it becomes `Float`;
non-finite values are rejected. Objects preserve key order and a repeated key keeps
the last value. Invalid input (bad escapes, trailing characters, nesting deeper than
16) returns `nil`; a valid JSON `null` also returns `nil`. Use `parseResult` when the
caller must distinguish malformed text from a valid `null`.

sections.title: fn parseResult(text: String) -> JsonResult
sections.text:
### `fn parseResult(text: String) -> JsonResult`

Parses JSON text, preserving the difference between `null` and invalid text.

Returns `JsonResult.Ok(nil)` for the JSON literal `null` and `JsonResult.Err(message)`
for malformed input, including the 16-level nesting cap. The message is the same one
`parse` used to hide and never contains a path, timestamp or address.

Returns `true` when `result` came from a valid JSON text.

Exists because an enum type exported by a module cannot be named in another module's
annotations; callers use these helpers instead of writing a typed wrapper function.

## Classes

### `class RpcFailure`

Why `decode` rejected a message; `code` is the JSON-RPC error code.

Error data is not stored because a field of type `Any` is not supported by the
backend; callers that need `error.data` build the envelope themselves.

#### `val code: Int`

Numeric JSON-RPC error code: `-32700` parse, `-32600` invalid request,
`-32601` method not found, `-32602` invalid params, `-32603` internal.

#### `val message: String`

Human-readable reason; never contains a path, timestamp or address.

#### `fn init(code: Int, message: String)`

Creates a failure with an explicit code and message.

sections.text:
## Functions

### `fn decode(text: String) -> Result[Map[String, Any], RpcFailure]`

Parses and validates one JSON-RPC 2.0 envelope.

A request has `method` and `id`; a notification has `method` and no `id`; a response
has exactly one of `result` or `error`. `id` is `Int` or `String` in requests, and
may also be `nil` in responses. `params` is an array or an object when present.
Batches (a top-level array) and malformed JSON are reported as failures.

### `fn encode(message: Map[String, Any]) -> String`

Serializes an envelope as compact JSON, preserving key insertion order.

### `fn request(id: Any, method: String, params: Any = ...) -> Map[String, Any]`

Builds a request with `method`, an `id` and optional `params`.

`id` should be an `Int` or a `String`; builders do not validate, `decode` does.

### `fn notification(method: String, params: Any = ...) -> Map[String, Any]`

Builds a notification: `method` with no `id`.

### `fn success(id: Any, result: Any = ...) -> Map[String, Any]`

Builds a success response; `result` may be `nil` (serialized as `null`).

### `fn failure(id: Any, code: Int, message: String) -> Map[String, Any]`

Builds an error response; the `error` object carries `code` and `message`.

### `fn isRequest(message: Map[String, Any]) -> Bool`

Returns `true` when the envelope is a request (has `method` and `id`).

### `fn isNotification(message: Map[String, Any]) -> Bool`

Returns `true` when the envelope is a notification (has `method` and no `id`).

### `fn isResponse(message: Map[String, Any]) -> Bool`

Returns `true` when the envelope is a response (has `result` or `error`).

### `fn hasId(message: Map[String, Any]) -> Bool`

Returns `true` when the `id` member is present (its value may be `nil`).

### `fn idOf(message: Map[String, Any]) -> Any`

Returns the `id` member, or `nil` when it is absent.

### `fn methodOf(message: Map[String, Any]) -> String | Nil`

Returns the `method` member, or `nil` when it is absent or not a string.

### `fn errorOf(message: Map[String, Any]) -> Map[String, Any] | Nil`

Returns the `error` object, or `nil` when it is absent or not an object.

pages.title: std.lists
pages.summary: Generic list combinators; every function leaves the input unchanged.

sections.title: API
sections.text: ## API

sections.title: Functions
sections.text:
## Functions

### `fn isEmpty(xs: List[Any]) -> Bool`

Returns `true` when the list has no elements.

### `fn length(xs: List[Any]) -> Int`

Returns the number of elements; equivalent to `len(xs)`.

### `fn map[T, U](xs: List[T], f: fn(T) -> U) -> List[U]`

Applies `f` to each element and returns the results in order.

The result has the same length as `xs`; the input list is not modified.

### `fn filter[T](xs: List[T], predicate: fn(T) -> Bool) -> List[T]`

Returns the elements for which `predicate` is true.

Preserves the original order and calls `predicate` once per element.

### `fn each[T](xs: List[T], action: fn(T) -> Nil) -> Nil`

Calls `action` for each element in order and returns `nil`.

Intended for side effects; the input list is not modified.

### `fn fold[T, U](xs: List[T], initial: U, f: fn(U, T) -> U) -> U`

Folds the list left to right starting from `initial`.

The accumulator type `U` may differ from the element type `T`.

### `fn any[T](xs: List[T], predicate: fn(T) -> Bool) -> Bool`

Returns true when at least one element satisfies `predicate`.

Stops at the first match; an empty list returns `false`.

### `fn all[T](xs: List[T], predicate: fn(T) -> Bool) -> Bool`

Returns true when every element satisfies `predicate`.

Stops at the first mismatch; an empty list satisfies it vacuously.

### `fn none[T](xs: List[T], predicate: fn(T) -> Bool) -> Bool`

Returns true when no element satisfies `predicate`.

Equivalent to `not any(xs, predicate)`.

### `fn findIndex[T](xs: List[T], predicate: fn(T) -> Bool) -> Int`

Returns the index of the first element satisfying `predicate`, or -1.

### `fn contains[T](xs: List[T], value: T) -> Bool`

Returns whether the list contains `value`.

Uses `==`, so lists, maps and tuples compare structurally.

### `fn indexOf[T](xs: List[T], value: T) -> Int`

Returns the first index where `value` occurs, or -1.

### `fn reverse[T](xs: List[T]) -> List[T]`

Returns a new list in reverse order without modifying the input.

### `fn take[T](xs: List[T], count: Int) -> List[T]`

Returns up to `count` elements from the start.

A zero or negative `count` yields `[]`; a `count` larger than the list yields a copy
of the whole list.

### `fn drop[T](xs: List[T], count: Int) -> List[T]`

Returns the list without its first `count` elements.

A negative `count` is treated as 0, so the whole list is returned.

### `fn slice[T](xs: List[T], start: Int, end: Int) -> List[T]`

Returns the half-open range `[start, end)`.

Indices are clamped: negatives become 0, `end < start` yields `[]`, and `end` beyond
the list length is clamped to `len(xs)`.

### `fn sum(xs: List[Int]) -> Int`

Returns the sum of all integers, or 0 for an empty list.

### `fn first[T](xs: List[T]) -> T | Nil`

Returns the first element, or `nil` when empty.

### `fn last[T](xs: List[T]) -> T | Nil`

Returns the last element, or `nil` when empty.

### `fn find[T](xs: List[T], predicate: fn(T) -> Bool) -> T | Nil`

Returns the first element that satisfies `predicate`, or `nil` when none matches.

### `fn reduce[T](xs: List[T], f: fn(T, T) -> T) -> T | Nil`

Reduces the list left to right using the first element as the accumulator.

Returns `nil` for an empty list. `f` receives `(accumulator, next)`.

### `fn count[T](xs: List[T], predicate: fn(T) -> Bool) -> Int`

Returns how many elements satisfy `predicate`.

### `fn min[T](xs: List[T]) -> T | Nil`

Returns the smallest element using `<`, or `nil` when empty.

### `fn max[T](xs: List[T]) -> T | Nil`

Returns the largest element using `>`, or `nil` when empty.

### `fn getOr[T](xs: List[T], index: Int, fallback: T) -> T`

Returns the element at `index`, or `fallback` when out of range.

Negative indices are out of range; there is no wrap-around.

### `fn sort[T](xs: List[T], compare: fn(T, T) -> Int) -> List[T]`

Returns a new list sorted by `compare`.

`compare(a, b)` returns a negative number when `a` comes first, zero for ties and a
positive number otherwise. The merge sort is stable and does not mutate the input.

### `fn sortNatural[T](xs: List[T]) -> List[T]`

Returns a new list sorted by natural ordering (`<=`).

Stable merge sort requiring `T: Ord`; the input list is not modified.

### `fn zip[T, U](xs: List[T], ys: List[U]) -> List[(T, U)]`

Pairs elements from both lists, stopping at the shorter one.

### `fn flatten[T](xs: List[List[T]]) -> List[T]`

Concatenates a list of lists into a new flat list, preserving order.

### `fn flatMap[T, U](xs: List[T], f: fn(T) -> List[U]) -> List[U]`

Maps each element to a list with `f` and concatenates the results.

### `fn unique[T](xs: List[T]) -> List[T]`

Returns the elements without duplicates, preserving first-occurrence order.

Uses structural equality and does not mutate the input.

### `fn chunk[T](xs: List[T], size: Int) -> List[List[T]]`

Splits the list into consecutive chunks of at most `size` elements.

The last chunk may be shorter. A `size` of 0 or less returns `[]`; each chunk is a
new list.

### `fn partition[T](xs: List[T], predicate: fn(T) -> Bool) -> (List[T], List[T])`

Splits the list into `(matching, rest)`.

Both lists preserve the original order, and `predicate` is called once per element.

sections.title: API
sections.text: ## API

sections.title: Classes
sections.text:
## Classes

### `class Logger`

Logger that writes to stderr and filters out levels below `minimum`.

#### `var minimum: Level`

Lowest level that will be written.

#### `fn init(minimum: Level | Nil = ...)`

Creates a logger; without an argument the minimum is `Level.Info`.

pages.title: std.maps
pages.summary: Helpers for Map[String, V] that preserve insertion order.

sections.title: API
sections.text: ## API

sections.title: Functions
sections.text:
## Functions

### `fn entries[V](m: Map[String, V]) -> List[(String, V)]`

Returns the key/value pairs in insertion order.

Each entry is a `(key, value)` tuple; the input map is not modified.

### `fn toList[V](m: Map[String, V]) -> List[(String, V)]`

Returns the key/value pairs in insertion order.

Alias of `entries`.

### `fn fromEntries[V](items: List[(String, V)]) -> Map[String, V]`

Builds a map from `(key, value)` pairs.

Later pairs with the same key win, while the key keeps its first insertion position.

### `fn merge[V](left: Map[String, V], right: Map[String, V]) -> Map[String, V]`

Merges two maps; the right-hand value wins.

Keys keep their first insertion position and `left` is not modified.

### `fn pick[V](m: Map[String, V], keys: List[String]) -> Map[String, V]`

Returns a map containing only the named keys that exist in `m`.

Output order follows `keys`, not the input map; duplicate names are ignored.

### `fn omit[V](m: Map[String, V], keys: List[String]) -> Map[String, V]`

Returns a map without the named keys, preserving the input order.

### `fn mapValues[V, U](m: Map[String, V], f: fn(V) -> U) -> Map[String, U]`

Transforms each value with `f`, preserving keys and insertion order.

### `fn filterKeys[V](m: Map[String, V], predicate: fn(String) -> Bool) -> Map[String, V]`

Keeps entries whose key satisfies `predicate`, preserving order.

### `fn filterValues[V](m: Map[String, V], predicate: fn(V) -> Bool) -> Map[String, V]`

Keeps entries whose value satisfies `predicate`, preserving order.

### `fn invert(m: Map[String, String]) -> Map[String, String]`

Swaps keys and values; later collisions win.

Requires `Map[String, String]`. When two keys share a value, the later key becomes
the surviving key and keeps the position of the first value insertion.

### `fn hasValue[V](m: Map[String, V], value: V) -> Bool`

Returns whether any value equals `value`, using structural equality.

### `fn getOr[V](m: Map[String, V], key: String, fallback: V) -> V`

Returns the value for `key`, or `fallback` when absent.

pages.title: std.numeric
pages.summary: Integer number theory and population statistics.

sections.title: API
sections.text: ## API

sections.title: Functions
sections.text:
## Functions

### `fn gcd(left: Int, right: Int) -> Int`

Returns the non-negative greatest common divisor.

Signs are ignored and `gcd(0, 0)` is 0.

### `fn lcm(left: Int, right: Int) -> Int`

Returns the non-negative least common multiple.

Returns 0 when either argument is 0; a large product can wrap like any `Int` product.

### `fn isPrime(value: Int) -> Bool`

Returns whether the integer is prime.

Values below 2 are not prime; 2 is prime and larger even numbers are rejected early.

### `fn primes(limit: Int) -> List[Int]`

Returns all primes up to and including `limit`, in ascending order.

`limit < 2` yields `[]`.

### `fn factorial(value: Int) -> Int`

Returns `value!`.

Negative input raises `RuntimeError`; an overflowing result wraps like any `Int`
product.

### `fn powMod(base: Int, exponent: Int, modulus: Int) -> Int`

Returns `base ** exponent` modulo `modulus`.

`modulus` must be positive and `exponent` non-negative, otherwise `RuntimeError` is
raised. A negative `base` is normalized before the modular arithmetic.

### `fn digitSum(value: Int) -> Int`

Returns the sum of the decimal digits.

The sign is ignored, so `digitSum(-42)` is 6; `digitSum(0)` is 0.

### `fn isEven(value: Int) -> Bool`

Returns whether the integer is even. Negative values follow the same parity rule.

### `fn isOdd(value: Int) -> Bool`

Returns whether the integer is odd. Negative values follow the same parity rule.

### `fn sign(value: Int) -> Int`

Returns -1, 0 or 1 according to the sign.

### `fn mean(values: List[Int]) -> Float | Nil`

Returns the arithmetic mean as `Float`, or `nil` for an empty list.

### `fn median(values: List[Int]) -> Float | Nil`

Returns the median as `Float`, or `nil` for an empty list.

A copy is sorted, so the input list is not modified. For an even length the two
middle values are averaged.

### `fn mode(values: List[Int]) -> Int | Nil`

Returns the most frequent value, or `nil` for an empty list.

Ties keep the value that first reaches the highest count in list order.

### `fn variance(values: List[Int]) -> Float | Nil`

Returns the population variance, or `nil` for an empty list.

Divides by n, not by n-1.

### `fn stddev(values: List[Int]) -> Float | Nil`

Returns the population standard deviation, or `nil` for an empty list.

Square root of `variance`.

### `fn roundTo(value: Float, digits: Int) -> Float`

Rounds to `digits` decimal places.

Negative digits are allowed and round to tens, hundreds and so on, because the scale
is `10.0 ** digits`.

### `fn toBase(value: Int, base: Int) -> String`

Formats an integer in base 2..36 using lowercase digits.

Negative values keep a leading `-`; an invalid base raises `RuntimeError`.

### `fn fromBase(text: String, base: Int) -> Int | Nil`

Parses an integer in base 2..36, returning `nil` when invalid.

Accepts an optional `+`/`-` and lowercase or uppercase digits. An invalid base raises
`RuntimeError`; invalid digits or an empty string return `nil`.

pages.title: std.paths
pages.summary: Lexical POSIX path helpers; no filesystem access.

sections.title: API
sections.text: ## API

sections.title: Functions
sections.text:
## Functions

### `fn isAbsolute(path: String) -> Bool`

Returns whether the POSIX path is absolute.

A path is absolute when its first code point is `/`; the empty string is relative.

### `fn split(path: String) -> List[String]`

Splits a POSIX path into components.

Splits on `/` and drops empty components, so repeated and leading/trailing
separators disappear: `split("/a//b/")` is `["a", "b"]` and `split("")` is `[]`.

### `fn joinPath(base: String, child: String) -> String`

Joins a base path and a child path with a single `/` separator.

An absolute `child` (or an empty `base`) wins and is returned unchanged. An empty
`child` returns `base`. This is a lexical join: `.` and `..` are not resolved and
separators already present in `child` are preserved.

### `fn basename(path: String) -> String`

Returns the final path component.

Trailing separators are ignored. `/` is its own basename and the empty path maps
to `.`; `basename("a/b/")` is `"b"`.

### `fn dirname(path: String) -> String`

Returns the parent path without a trailing separator.

`dirname("/a")` is `/`, `dirname("a")` and the empty path are `.`. The result is
lexical: no filesystem lookup or symlink resolution happens.

### `fn ext(path: String) -> String`

Returns the file extension of the final component, without the leading dot.

`ext("a/b.tar.gz")` is `"gz"`; a dotfile such as `.bashrc` has no extension, and a
missing extension returns `""`.

### `fn stem(path: String) -> String`

Returns the final component without its extension.

`stem("a/b.tar.gz")` is `"b.tar"`; a name without an extension is returned
unchanged, and dotfiles such as `.bashrc` keep their leading dot.

### `fn normalize(path: String) -> String`

Resolves `.` and `..` lexically, collapsing repeated separators.

Absolute paths keep their leading `/`; `..` above a relative root is preserved, so
`normalize("a/../..")` is `".."`. The empty path normalizes to `.`. No filesystem
access and no symlink resolution: the result depends only on the input text.

sections.title: API
sections.text: ## API

sections.title: Classes
sections.text:
## Classes

### `class ProcError`

Host failure of a process operation.

#### `val kind: String`

Stable token: `spawnFailed`, `closed`, `pipeClosed`, `timeout`, `io`.

#### `val message: String`

Human-readable detail; no PID, path or locale text.

#### `fn init(kind: String, message: String)`

Builds a failure from a stable kind and a message.

### `class Stream`

Byte stream of a child process (`stdin`, `stdout` or `stderr`).

#### `val id: Int`

Stream handle used by `proc.*`.

#### `fn init(id: Int)`

Wraps an existing stream handle.

#### `fn read(n: Int) -> Result[String | Nil, ProcError]`

Reads up to `n` bytes, or `Ok(nil)` at end of stream.

Reading stops at a UTF-8 boundary, so the returned text is always valid even when
`n` lands inside a multi-byte code point.

#### `fn write(text: String) -> Result[Nil, ProcError]`

Writes all text; `pipeClosed` when the other side closed the pipe.

#### `fn close() -> Result[Nil, ProcError]`

Closes the descriptor; closing twice is a no-op.

### `class Process`

Child process with its three channels connected to pipes.

#### `val id: Int`

Process handle used by `proc.*`.

#### `val stdin: Stream`

Child's standard input.

#### `val stdout: Stream`

Child's standard output.

#### `val stderr: Stream`

Child's standard error.

#### `fn init(id: Int)`

Wraps an already-started process handle; prefer `spawn`.

#### `fn wait() -> Result[Int, ProcError]`

Waits for the process to exit and returns its status.

A negative status means the child was terminated by a signal.

#### `fn kill() -> Bool`

Sends `SIGKILL`, returning `false` when the process already exited.

#### `fn close() -> Result[Nil, ProcError]`

Closes the channels and releases the handle; closing twice is a no-op.

### `class Output`

Captured output of a finished `run`.

#### `val code: Int`

Exit code (negative when the child died from a signal).

#### `val stdout: String`

Everything the child wrote to stdout.

#### `val stderr: String`

Everything the child wrote to stderr.

#### `fn init(code: Int, stdout: String, stderr: String)`

Builds the result of a finished run.

## Functions

### `fn spawn(argv: List[String]) -> Result[Process, ProcError]`

Starts `argv` without a shell, with pipes on all three channels.

`argv[0]` is resolved by the OS, not by a shell, so no quoting or command
interpolation happens.

### `fn run(argv: List[String], stdin: String = ..., timeoutMs: Int = ...) -> Result[Output, ProcError]`

Runs `argv` to completion and returns its exit code and captured output.

`stdin` is written before the first `poll` (practical limit: the pipe buffer,
~64 KiB; larger text can block if the child does not read). `timeoutMs > 0` kills the
process and returns `Err(ProcError("timeout", ...))`. There is no shell.

sections.text:
## Functions

### `fn forAll[T](generator: Gen[T], check: fn(T) -> Nil, runs: Int = ..., seed: Int = ...) -> Nil`

Runs `check` with `runs` generated values; on failure shrinks and raises.

Stops at the first failure and raises `TestFailure` with the run number, seed,
original counterexample and shrunk value. `Skip` propagates unchanged. `seed` is
explicit, so a failing run is reproducible.

### `fn int() -> Gen[Int]`

64-bit integer generator; shrinks toward 0 and then toward the halfway point.

### `fn intRange(min: Int, max: Int) -> Gen[Int]`

Integer generator in `[min, max]`; shrinks toward `min`.

### `fn bool() -> Gen[Bool]`

`Bool` generator; shrinks `true` to `false`.

### `fn float() -> Gen[Float]`

`Float` generator in `[0.0, 1.0)`; shrinks to `0.0`.

### `fn listOf[T](element: Gen[T], maxLength: Int = ...) -> Gen[List[T]]`

List generator with length in `[0, maxLength]`; shrinks by removing elements.

Elements are drawn from `element`; shrunk lists are not shrunk element-wise.

### `fn listOfInt(element: Gen[Int], maxLength: Int = ...) -> Gen[List[Int]]`

List of `Int`; compatibility alias of `listOf`.

### `fn listOfString(element: Gen[String], maxLength: Int = ...) -> Gen[List[String]]`

List of `String`; compatibility alias of `listOf`.

### `fn stringOf(maxLength: Int = ...) -> Gen[String]`

String generator over `[a-z0-9]` with length in `[0, maxLength]`.

Shrinks by deleting one character per candidate.

### `fn oneOf[T](options: List[T]) -> Gen[T]`

Chooses one value from `options`; shrinks toward the first element.

Raises `RuntimeError` when `options` is empty.

pages.title: std.rand
pages.summary: Deterministic xorshift64* PRNG with an explicit seed.

sections.title: API
sections.text: ## API

sections.title: Classes
sections.text:
## Classes

### `class Rand`

Deterministic xorshift64* generator; the same seed yields the same sequence.

#### `var state: Int`

Internal state (never zero).

#### `fn init(seed: Int)`

Creates a generator; `seed == 0` maps to the fixed default state.

The seed is the only source of variation, so sequences are reproducible.

#### `fn reseed(seed: Int) -> Nil`

Restarts the sequence with `seed`; `0` maps to the same default as `init`.

#### `fn nextInt() -> Int`

Returns the next raw 64-bit value.

The `Int` may be negative; use `int` or `float` for bounded values.

#### `fn int(min: Int, max: Int) -> Int`

Returns an integer in `[min, max]` (inclusive).

Raises `RuntimeError` when `min > max` or when the span overflows an `Int`.

#### `fn float() -> Float`

Returns a `Float` in `[0.0, 1.0)` with 53 bits of mantissa.

#### `fn bool() -> Bool`

Returns `true` or `false` with equal probability.

## Functions

### `fn isOk[T, E](result: Result[T, E]) -> Bool`

Returns `true` for `Result.Ok` and `false` for `Result.Err`.

### `fn isErr[T, E](result: Result[T, E]) -> Bool`

Returns `true` for `Result.Err` and `false` for `Result.Ok`.

### `fn map[T, U, E](result: Result[T, E], transform: fn(T) -> U) -> Result[U, E]`

Applies `transform` to the success value; an error passes through unchanged.

The error type `E` is preserved.

### `fn mapErr[T, E, F](result: Result[T, E], transform: fn(E) -> F) -> Result[T, F]`

Applies `transform` to the error value; a success passes through unchanged.

The success type `T` is preserved.

### `fn errorOf[T, E](result: Result[T, E]) -> E | Nil`

Returns the error value, or `nil` when the result is a success.

### `fn unwrapOr[T, E](result: Result[T, E], fallback: T) -> T`

Returns the success value, or `fallback` for an error.

`fallback` is an ordinary argument, so it is evaluated before the call.

### `fn andThen[T, U, E](result: Result[T, E], transform: fn(T) -> Result[U, E]) -> Result[U, E]`

Chains a computation that itself returns a `Result`.

On success `transform` is called; on error the original error is returned unchanged.
This is the monadic bind for `Result`.

### `fn toOptional[T, E](result: Result[T, E]) -> T | Nil`

Returns the success value, or `nil` when the result is an error.

The error value is discarded; use `match` when it must be inspected.

### `class Set[T]`

Mutable set backed by `Map[Any, Bool]`.

#### `val items: Map[Any, Bool]`

Backing map; keys are elements and every value is `true`.

#### `fn init()`

Creates an empty set.

#### `fn add(value: T) -> Nil`

Adds `value`; adding an existing value is a no-op that keeps its position.

#### `fn has(value: T) -> Bool`

Returns whether `value` is in the set.

#### `fn remove(value: T) -> Bool`

Removes `value`, returning whether it was present.

#### `fn len() -> Int`

Returns the number of elements.

#### `fn toList() -> List[T]`

Returns the elements as a list in insertion order.

#### `fn union(other: Set[T]) -> Set[T]`

Returns a new set with the elements of both sets.

Elements of `this` come first, followed by new elements of `other`.

#### `fn intersect(other: Set[T]) -> Set[T]`

Returns a new set with the elements present in both sets.

Order follows `this`.

#### `fn difference(other: Set[T]) -> Set[T]`

Returns a new set with the elements of `this` that are not in `other`.

Order follows `this`.
