pages.title: std.strings
pages.summary: UTF-8 text operations over code points, not bytes or UTF-16 units.

sections.title: API
sections.text: ## API

sections.title: Functions
sections.text:
## Functions

### `fn isEmpty(s: String) -> Bool`

Returns `true` when the string has no characters.

### `fn isBlank(s: String) -> Bool`

Returns `true` when the string is empty or contains only whitespace.

Whitespace is space, tab, LF and CR, the same set used by `trim` and `words`.

### `fn ltrim(s: String) -> String`

Removes leading whitespace (space, tab, LF or CR).

### `fn rtrim(s: String) -> String`

Removes trailing whitespace (space, tab, LF or CR).

### `fn trim(s: String) -> String`

Removes leading and trailing whitespace (space, tab, LF or CR).

### `fn startsWith(s: String, prefix: String) -> Bool`

Returns whether the string starts with `prefix`.

An empty prefix always matches; a longer prefix never matches.

### `fn endsWith(s: String, suffix: String) -> Bool`

Returns whether the string ends with `suffix`.

An empty suffix always matches; a longer suffix never matches.

### `fn indexOf(s: String, needle: String) -> Int`

Returns the first code-point index of `needle`, or -1.

An empty needle matches at index 0. Indices count code points, not bytes.

### `fn lastIndexOf(s: String, needle: String) -> Int`

Returns the last code-point index of `needle`, or -1.

An empty needle returns `len(s)`. Indices count code points, not bytes.

### `fn contains(s: String, needle: String) -> Bool`

Returns whether the string contains `needle`; an empty needle is always contained.

### `fn split(s: String, separator: String) -> List[String]`

Splits on each occurrence of `separator`.

An empty separator splits into code points (`chars(s)`). Otherwise empty fields are
preserved: `split("a,,b", ",")` is `["a", "", "b"]`.

### `fn splitLines(s: String) -> List[String]`

Splits into lines on LF or CRLF.

A trailing newline produces a final empty line; `std.fs.readLines` drops it for file
input. A bare CR is not a line break here.

### `fn lines(s: String) -> List[String]`

Alias of `splitLines`; splits on LF or CRLF.

### `fn words(s: String) -> List[String]`

Splits on runs of whitespace, ignoring empty fields.

Leading and trailing whitespace is discarded, so `words("  a  b ")` is `["a", "b"]`.

### `fn repeat(s: String, count: Int) -> String`

Repeats the string `count` times.

A zero or negative count yields `""`.

### `fn upper(s: String) -> String`

Returns an uppercase copy.

Only ASCII `a-z` is mapped; other code points are copied unchanged (no Unicode case
folding).

### `fn lower(s: String) -> String`

Returns a lowercase copy.

Only ASCII `A-Z` is mapped; other code points are copied unchanged (no Unicode case
folding).

### `fn capitalize(s: String) -> String`

Uppercases the first code point and lowercases the rest.

Only ASCII letters change; an empty string is returned unchanged.

### `fn reverse(s: String) -> String`

Reverses by code points.

Combining marks and grapheme clusters are not handled specially: each code point is
moved independently.

### `fn count(s: String, needle: String) -> Int`

Counts non-overlapping occurrences of `needle`.

An empty needle returns 0.

### `fn replaceFirst(s: String, old: String, new: String) -> String`

Replaces the first occurrence of `old`.

Returns `s` unchanged when `old` is absent. An empty `old` matches at index 0, so
`new` is inserted before the text.

### `fn replaceAll(s: String, old: String, new: String) -> String`

Replaces every non-overlapping occurrence of `old`.

An empty `old` returns `s` unchanged, avoiding an infinite insertion.

### `fn slice(s: String, start: Int, end: Int) -> String`

Returns the half-open range `[start, end)`.

Indices are clamped: negatives become 0, `end < start` yields `""`, and `end` beyond
the string length is clamped to `len(s)`.

### `fn padStart(s: String, width: Int, fill: String) -> String`

Pads on the left with repeated `fill` to `width`.

If `s` is already at least `width` long, or `fill` is empty, `s` is returned
unchanged. The padding is truncated to the exact gap.

### `fn padEnd(s: String, width: Int, fill: String) -> String`

Pads on the right with repeated `fill` to `width`.

If `s` is already at least `width` long, or `fill` is empty, `s` is returned
unchanged. The padding is truncated to the exact width.

pages.title: std.test
pages.summary: Mini test harness with TAP output, hooks, matchers and a recorder.

sections.title: API
sections.text: ## API

sections.title: Classes
sections.text:
## Classes

### `class TestFailure(Exception)`

Test failure (distinct from `RuntimeError`, which is an infrastructure bug).

#### `fn init(message: String)`

Creates the failure with the message shown in the report.

### `class Skip(Exception)`

Test skipped on purpose; the runner counts it as `skip`, not as a failure.

#### `fn init(reason: String)`

Creates the skip with the given reason.

### `class Suite`

Test suite: `describe`, `it`, `report` and `done`.

#### `var total: Int`

Number of tests executed (filtered-out tests do not count).

#### `var passed: Int`

Tests that passed.

#### `var failed: Int`

Tests that failed.

#### `var skipped: Int`

Tests skipped with `skip`.

#### `var prefixes: List[String]`

Group names opened by `describe`, innermost last.

#### `var filter: String`

Substring filter read from `--filter=` in the script arguments.

#### `var only: String`

Exact test name read from `--only=` in the script arguments.

#### `var beforeHooks: List[fn() -> Nil]`

Hooks run before each `it`, in registration order.

#### `var afterHooks: List[fn() -> Nil]`

Hooks run after each `it`, in reverse registration order.

#### `var listMode: Bool`

`--list`: print `# test <name>` only, without executing (per-test isolation).

#### `var protocol: Bool`

`--protocol=json`: emit framed events instead of TAP (machine protocol).

#### `var token: String`

Nonce prefix for control lines; prevents user `print` from spoofing events.

#### `fn init()`

Creates an empty suite and reads `--filter=`/`--only=` from `args()`.

Also detects `--list`, `--protocol=json` and `--token=`.

#### `fn describe(name: String, body: fn() -> Nil) -> Nil`

Opens a group; its name prefixes every `it` and its hooks apply only here.

Hooks registered inside the body are removed when the body returns.

#### `fn beforeEach(body: fn() -> Nil) -> Nil`

Registers a hook run before each `it` in this `describe`.

#### `fn afterEach(body: fn() -> Nil) -> Nil`

Registers a hook run after each `it` in this `describe`.

#### `fn it(name: String, body: fn() -> Nil) -> Nil`

Runs a test immediately and prints `ok`/`not ok` in TAP.

Filtered tests do not run or count. A skipped test still counts in `total` but not
as passed or failed. A failure in `beforeEach`/`afterEach` is reported as a test
failure.

#### `fn skip(reason: String) -> Nil`

Skips the current test with `reason`.

Raises `Skip`, which `it` turns into a `# SKIP` line rather than a failure.

#### `fn report() -> Int`

Prints the TAP plan and summary, returning 0 (all passed) or 1 (any failure).

In protocol mode it emits the `end` event and stays silent instead.

#### `fn done() -> Nil`

Calls `report()` and exits the process with its code.

In `--list` mode it exits 0 immediately.

### `class Expectation[T]`

Equality assertion for a concrete value (scalar, string, list, map or tuple).

#### `val value: T`

Observed value.

#### `fn init(value: T)`

Wraps the observed value.

#### `fn toBe(other: T) -> Nil`

Fails when `value != other`.

#### `fn notToBe(other: T) -> Nil`

Fails when `value == other`.

### `class ListExpectation[T]`

Assertion over the elements of a list.

#### `val items: List[T]`

Observed list.

#### `fn init(items: List[T])`

Wraps the observed list.

#### `fn toContain(item: T) -> Nil`

Fails when `item` is not in the list (structural equality).

### `class StringExpectation`

Assertion over the contents of a string.

#### `val text: String`

Observed text.

#### `fn init(text: String)`

Wraps the observed text.

#### `fn contains(needle: String) -> Nil`

Fails when `text` does not contain `needle`.

### `class Recorder`

Records calls of a spy/fake: `record`, `count`, `order` and `clear`.

#### `val calls: List[String]`

Calls in registration order.

#### `fn init()`

Creates an empty recorder.

#### `fn record(name: String) -> Nil`

Records one call by name.

#### `fn count(name: String) -> Int`

Returns how many times `name` was recorded.

#### `fn order() -> List[String]`

Returns a copy of the calls in registration order.

#### `fn clear() -> Nil`

Empties the record.

sections.title: Functions
sections.text:
## Functions

### `fn fail(message: String) -> Nil`

Fails the current test with `message`.

### `fn expect[T](value: T) -> Expectation[T]`

Wraps a concrete value for `toBe`/`notToBe`.

### `fn expectGt[T](actual: T, expected: T) -> Nil`

Fails when `actual <= expected` (natural order of `T: Ord`).

### `fn expectGe[T](actual: T, expected: T) -> Nil`

Fails when `actual < expected`.

### `fn expectLt[T](actual: T, expected: T) -> Nil`

Fails when `actual >= expected`.

### `fn expectLe[T](actual: T, expected: T) -> Nil`

Fails when `actual > expected`.

### `fn expectNil[T](value: T | Nil) -> Nil`

Fails when `value` is not `nil`.

Pass a typed optional (`val x: Int? = nil`): `expectNil(nil)` is a nested optional and
the backend rejects it.

### `fn expectNotNil[T](value: T | Nil) -> T`

Fails when `value` is `nil`; returns the narrowed value.

### `fn expectList[T](items: List[T]) -> ListExpectation[T]`

Wraps a list for `toContain`.

### `fn expectString(text: String) -> StringExpectation`

Wraps a string for `contains`.

### `fn expectRaise(body: fn() -> Nil) -> String`

Runs `body` and returns the exception message; fails when nothing is raised.

Catches any `Exception`, including `Skip` and `TestFailure`.

sections.title: Functions
sections.text:
## Functions

### `fn daysFromCivil(year: Int, month: Int, day: Int) -> Int`

Returns days since 1970-01-01 for a civil date.

Uses Howard Hinnant's proleptic-Gregorian algorithm. `month` is 1..12 and `day` is
1..31; invalid combinations are not rejected here (use `date` for that).

### `fn civilFromDays(days: Int) -> (Int, Int, Int)`

Returns `(year, month, day)` for days since 1970-01-01.

Inverse of `daysFromCivil` and likewise proleptic Gregorian.

### `fn isLeapYear(year: Int) -> Bool`

Returns whether `year` is a leap year in the proleptic Gregorian calendar.

### `fn daysInMonth(year: Int, month: Int) -> Int`

Returns the number of days in `month` of `year` (28..31).

`month` is expected to be 1..12; the result is undefined outside that range.

### `fn date(year: Int, month: Int, day: Int) -> Result[(Int, Int, Int), TimeError]`

Validates a civil date and returns it as `(year, month, day)`.

`year` must be 0..9999 (the formatting range), `month` 1..12 and `day` within the
month. Invalid input is `Result.Err(TimeError("invalidDate", ...))`.

### `fn iso(ms: Int) -> String`

Formats an instant (milliseconds since the epoch) as `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`.

Raises `RuntimeError` when the year falls outside 0..9999. The instant is floored
into its civil day and the milliseconds are truncated, so pre-epoch values still
format consistently (`-1` ms is `1969-12-31T23:59:59Z`).

### `fn isoMillis(ms: Int) -> String`

Formats an instant as `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.mmmZ`.

Like `iso`, but keeps the three millisecond digits (floored, so `-1` ms is
`1969-12-31T23:59:59.999Z`).

### `fn isoDate(ms: Int) -> String`

Formats the civil date of an instant as `YYYY-MM-DD`.

### `fn isoIn(ms: Int, offsetMinutes: Int) -> String`

Formats an instant in an explicit offset, e.g. `2024-01-01T00:00:00+03:00`.

`offsetMinutes` is `-720..840`; zero formats as `Z`. The instant is shifted before
formatting, so the civil fields are the local ones at that offset.

### `fn parts(ms: Int) -> (Int, Int, Int, Int, Int, Int)`

Splits an instant into `(year, month, day, hour, minute, second)` UTC.

Uses floor division, so instants before the epoch still produce a valid civil date;
milliseconds are dropped.

### `fn partsIn(ms: Int, offsetMinutes: Int) -> (Int, Int, Int, Int, Int, Int)`

Splits an instant into civil fields at an explicit offset.

`offsetMinutes` is `-720..840`; the returned fields are local to that offset.

### `fn weekday(ms: Int) -> Int`

Returns the ISO weekday of an instant: 1 = Monday … 7 = Sunday.

### `fn dayOfYear(ms: Int) -> Int`

Returns the day of the year of an instant: 1..365 (366 in a leap year).

### `fn addDays(ms: Int, days: Int) -> Int`

Adds `days` days of exactly 86.400.000 ms to an instant.

### `fn addMonths(ms: Int, months: Int) -> Int`

Adds calendar months to an instant, clamping the day to the target month.

The time of day is preserved. `2024-01-31 + 1 month` is `2024-02-29`, and
`2024-03-31 - 1 month` is `2024-02-29`; the operation is not invertible at month
ends (that is the price of a calendar month, not a 30-day duration).

### `fn addYears(ms: Int, years: Int) -> Int`

Adds calendar years to an instant, clamping 29 February in a non-leap year.

Equivalent to `addMonths(ms, years * 12)`.

### `fn diffDays(a: Int, b: Int) -> Int`

Returns the difference `a - b` in civil days (floor), not in 24 h periods.

### `fn parseIso(text: String) -> Int | Nil`

Parses an ISO-8601 instant string into milliseconds since the epoch.

Returns `nil` for malformed input; `parseIsoResult` preserves the cause.

### `fn parseIsoResult(text: String) -> Result[Int, TimeError]`

Parses an ISO-8601 instant, preserving the cause of a malformed input.

Accepts `YYYY-MM-DD` (midnight UTC) and
`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS[.mmm](https://loxia-lang.github.io/loxia/stdlib/Z|+HH:MM|-HH:MM/)`; `t`/`z` may be lowercase. The
fraction is 1..3 digits (`.5` is 500 ms) and more than three is rejected. Leap
seconds are not accepted: `second` must be 0..59. The returned instant is UTC.

sections.title: Functions
sections.text:
## Functions

### `fn byteLen(text: String) -> Int`

Counts the UTF-8 bytes of `text` (1..4 per code point).

### `fn utf16Len(text: String) -> Int`

Counts the UTF-16 code units of `text` (2 for code points above U+FFFF).

### `fn utf16Column(text: String, index: Int) -> Int`

Returns the UTF-16 width of the prefix of `index` code points.

`index` is clamped to 0..len(text), so negative and out-of-range values do not raise.
